• 楊氏は台湾ドルが今年、相対的に軟調となっていることについて、海外投資家による台湾株の利益確定売りが要因だと述べた。

• また、台湾の現在の外貨準備の８割は引き続き米債で保有しているとした。

item.title: ＮＹＳＥ、株バイナリーオプション開始へ 業績指標連動型も申請
item.description:
Laura Matthews
［ニューヨーク ２７日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）は、株式や上場...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹＳＥ、株バイナリーオプション開始へ　業績指標連動型も申請 14:05 配信

写真はＮＹＳＥの建物。2021年1月、米ニューヨーク市で撮影。 REUTERS/Mike Segar（ロイター） Laura Matthews

［ニューヨーク　２７日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）は、株式や上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）の満期日終値があらかじめ設定した価格を上回るか下回るかに対して、投資家が「オール・オア・ナッシング」の賭けを行える新たなオプション契約（バイナリー・リターン・オプション）の取引開始を準備している。

オプションやイベント連動型契約の取引が急増する中で、もっとピンポイントの予想をしたり、リスク管理をより精緻に行ったりしたい個人・機関投資家の需要を取り込むため、取引所各社が新商品開発を進めている事情がうかがえる。

ＮＹＳＥはまた、企業業績指標に連動する第２の新商品、バイナリー型の主要業績評価指標（ＫＰＩ）オプションについても承認を申請しており、イベントドリブン取引への旺盛な需要を取り込む動きを強めている。この商品は、企業が公表する業績指標が設定水準を上回るか下回るかに応じて投資家に利益を支払う仕組み。従来の株価連動型オプションとは異なり、ＫＰＩオプションでは売上高や１株利益、クラウド事業売上高、自動車生産台数などの指標そのものを対象に取引できる。

バイナリー・リターン・オプションは数日以内に取引が開始される見通し。対象となる原資産は１２銘柄で、アップル、エヌビディア、テスラ、ＳＰＤＲ・Ｓ＆Ｐ５００・ＥＴＦトラストなどが含まれる。対象銘柄は順次追加される予定だ。

ＮＹＳＥのケビン・タイレル最高プロダクト責任者は「ここ数年、米国のオプション市場は驚異的な成長を遂げている。取引量の増加を詳しく見ると、新しい取引手法や新商品に対する関心が高まっていることが分かる」と述べた。

これらの契約は現金決済型で、満期時にのみ権利行使できる欧州型を採用。対象指標が満期時に権利行使価格で定めた水準を満たした場合は１ドルを支払い、満たさなかった場合は、支払いは行われない。

ロイター 関連リンク コラム：ルラ氏勝利でトランプ氏の「ドンロー主義」打撃、中国の優位拡大か コラム：ＡＩ懸念や金利上昇、ＦＲＢにスタグフレーションの試練も アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か 10/28(水) 14:05 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: Rio Tinto proposes 56% pay jump for CEO as mining sector fights for talent
item.description: Rio Tinto's , board has proposed increasing its CEO Simon Trott's target remuneration package by 56% to £9.8 million ($13.06 million), according to four people familiar with the matter and documents reviewed by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Burton, Clara Denina
item.content:encoded: Rio Tinto's (RIO.AX) , (RIO.L) board has proposed increasing its CEO Simon Trott's target remuneration package by 56% to £9.8 million ($13.06 million), according to four people familiar with the matter and documents reviewed by Reuters. Surging pay at defence, aerospace and energy transition firms has left mining companies including Rio Tinto — the world's second-biggest listed miner — scrambling to compete for top talent. Rio Tinto's board has expanded its peer benchmarking group — the list of companies it compares itself to when calculating executive compensation ranges — an investor presentation seen by Reuters showed. Among other companies, it added US energy majors Chevron (CVX.N) and ExxonMobil (XOM.N) as well as GE Aerospace (GE.N) . Responding to Reuters questions about the changes, Ben Wyatt, who chairs Rio Tinto's remuneration committee, said the miner was consulting investors ahead of a policy update. He said Trott's fixed pay would remain unchanged but incentives tied to multiyear business outcomes and shareholder returns would be adjusted. "This is designed to drive business performance in the interests of shareholders, support the delivery of Rio Tinto's long-term strategy, and attract and retain strong leadership in a competitive global market," he said in a statement. Appointed in July 2025, Trott delivered a [USN:L4N43U2OW TEXT:"43% jump in first-half underlying earnings"] this year while pursuing restructuring and asset sales. SOME INVESTORS CONCERNED ABOUT CEO PAY INFLATION, BAD OPTICS Reflecting a compensation overhaul weighted to performance, Trott's maximum remuneration is proposed to grow 63% to £18.3 million, the briefing documents showed. Short-term incentives would rise to a maximum of 300% of base salary from 200%, while long-term targets would jump to 900% from 500%. Trott's new package would apply to the next three years of his compensation. To come into effect, the expanded framework will require shareholder approval at next year's annual meeting. Some Rio Tinto investors, however, told Reuters they were concerned the compensation proposal could fuel salary inflation among top Australian mining executives and, amid a cost-of-living crisis, reflect poorly on the company. GLOBAL RUSH TO SECURE TOP LEADERS DRIVES UP CEO PAY A Deloitte report in April showed that median CEO pay at FTSE 100 companies increased 18% year-on-year to £5.89 million in 2025. Executive pay in Britain's aerospace, engineering and manufacturing sectors in particular has surged in the past two years. And as competition for top leaders heats up — both across sectors and within a mining industry pivoting toward energy transition metals — mining executives are already moving or being approached. Rag Udd is leaving BHP (BHP.AX) to become CEO of Albemarle (ALB.N) , while French miner Eramet (ERMT.PA) approached Rio Tinto's Jerome Pecresse for its CEO position within the past year, according to one person close to the matter. Both Albemarle and Eramet are developing lithium projects for electric vehicle batteries. Pecresse, who Rio Tinto recruited from General Electric, did not respond to a request for comment. Eramet and Rio Tinto declined to comment. BRIDGING THE TRANSATLANTIC PAY GAP Companies outside the United States are also increasing pay to bridge a widening transatlantic divide. Nearly 60% of FTSE 350 companies proposed pay increases during this year's annual general meeting cycle, data from proxy advisory services firm Glass Lewis showed. Under Rio Tinto's proposed changes, Trott's maximum package would place him just under the median of the 19 companies the miner considers peers. US oil major ExxonMobil's CEO Darren Woods, who earned $33 million in 2025, topped that list, the documents showed. Canada's Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM.TO) and US miner Freeport-McMoRan (FCX.N) were the highest-ranked mining companies in the peer group. If approved, Trott's pay increase would put him among the top tier of Australian CEOs and ahead of rival miner BHP's Brandon Craig, whose remuneration is expected to be around $10 million and is capped at just below $13 million. Such pay gaps could put pressure on other companies to follow Rio Tinto's lead, investors and analysts say. Total median pay for CEOs and CFOs already jumped 14% this year through performance-linked incentives, according to a Bedford Group report on mining industry compensation. Yet some shareholder resistance remains. Last year, Anglo American (AAL.L) [USN:L4N3XE0FE TEXT:"withdrew a proposal"] to guarantee substantial bonuses for senior executives tied to its Teck Resources (TECKb.TO) merger. But others, including George Cheveley, portfolio manager at Rio Tinto shareholder Ninety One, said higher pay can be a useful tool to boost performance. "As long as it is aligned with shareholders, I'm quite happy," Cheveley said in response to a generic question about mining executive pay. ($1 = 0.7505 pounds)

item.title: Businesses and investors of Ambani's Jio as it debuts on Indian bourses
item.description: Jio Platforms shares soared 21% in their Mumbai debut on Wednesday, giving India's biggest-ever initial public offering a roaring start and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries its first listing in two decades.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jio Platforms (JIOP.NS) shares soared 21% in their Mumbai debut on Wednesday, giving India's biggest-ever initial public offering a roaring start and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries its first listing in two decades. The listing of the company, whose main business is telecoms, marks the first public listing from Reliance (RELI.NS) since 2006. Here are facts and numbers on Jio Platforms, which counts Meta (META.O) and Google among its major foreign investors: TELECOMS BUSINESS Reliance Jio Platforms is a unit of Ambani's oil-to-retail conglomerate Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) . It is best known for the telecom business Reliance Jio Infocomm, which is the country's biggest player with more than 500 million subscribers. Launched in 2016, the telecom business, popularly referred to simply as Jio, hit rivals such as Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) and Vodafone Idea (VODA.NS) hard by offering free voice and data plans initially. The move, in line with Ambani's [USN:L4N35S18O TEXT:"typical strategy"] of offering ultra-low prices to lure consumers, drove up its customer base and allowed many Indians to access platforms such as YouTube and Facebook for the first time. Jio says it currently has a roughly 60% share of India's data traffic. In recent years, Jio Platforms has diversified beyond the telecom sector into AI, cloud and enterprise network services, as well as app development. In 2023, Nvidia (NVDA.O) announced an AI [USN:L1N3AK0MB TEXT:"partnership"] with Reliance to develop cloud infrastructure and language models. THE LEADERSHIP Mukesh Ambani, one of Asia's richest men, is the chairman of Jio Platforms. His three children — [USN:L4N4670YX TEXT:"Akash"], Anant and Isha — serve on its board. Akash Ambani, his elder son, is the chairman of the company's flagship telecom unit, Reliance Jio Infocomm. Pankaj Pawar is the CEO of Jio Platforms. KEY FINANCIALS, VALUATION Reliance Jio Platforms' revenue from operations rose 14.6% to 1.47 trillion rupees ($15.45 billion) in the fiscal year ended March, while profit increased 15.1% to 300.49 billion Indian rupees ($3.16 billion). Around 90% of those figures were attributable to its telecoms business alone. MARQUEE INVESTORS In 2020, Jio Platforms raised more than $20.5 billion from 13 global investors in exchange for a roughly 33% equity stake, at a valuation range of $57 billion to $65 billion. Global names such as Meta Platforms (META.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and KKR (KKR.N) invested in the firm, as Ambani sought to turn Jio Platforms into the centerpiece of his technology ambitions. Other investors include General Atlantic, Silver Lake and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. Meta owns a 9.9% stake in the company, followed by Google's 7.7% stake. The Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity were among investors who bid in the anchor book of the IPO, which drew more than [USN:L4N4650J2 TEXT:"$25 billion in demand"]. THE IPO JOURNEY The filing, which had been targeted for as early as March, had been pushed back as IPO activity slowed following the outbreak of the Iran war, with investors losing their appetite for new listings. The company's shares started trading on October 28. It has been a long road to the IPO. In 2019, Ambani said Jio would "move towards" a listing within five years, and later the plans were delayed again in 2025. The company has hired [USN:L4N4060N2 TEXT:"19 banks"] to manage its offering.

item.title: 仏教員組合、政府の教育改革案は「不十分」 学生は抗議継続へ
item.description:
Dominique Vidalon
[パリ ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Dominique Vidalon

[パリ ２７日 ロイター] - フランスの教員組合ＳＮＥＳ─ＦＳＵは２７日、学生らが教育制度の改革などを求めて数週間続けている抗議活動について、政府の教育改革案は怒りを鎮めるには不十分だと指摘した。

政府は２６日、一部の学級の人数を２８人に制限する措置や校舎改修向けの融資、大学入学制度の見直しを発表した。これに対し、ＳＮＥＳ─ＦＳＵのソフィー・ベネティテ事務局長は、こうした措置を十分ではないとし、学習環境の改善には人数制限の対象拡大と教職員の増員が必要だと訴えた。

今回のデモは高校生による人員や教育資源の不足への抗議から始まり、労働組合や「黄色いベスト」運動にも拡大。公共サービスの弱体化や生活費上昇への不満を示す動きとなった。

アミエル予算相によると、対策費は５０億ユーロ（約５６億ドル）を見込み、他分野の歳出削減で相殺する。政府は債券市場から債務削減を求められ、財政的な余裕が乏しい。

学生の指導者らは政府案を第一歩と評価しつつ、今月３１日と１１月５日のデモ継続を表明。ヌニェス内相は、全国的な抗議活動が暴力や略奪に発展した事態を踏まえ、３１日は厳重な警備態勢を敷くと述べた。混乱は極右指導者ルペン氏への支持押し上げにつながっている。

item.title: Rays rally for 2 in 12th inning, extend World Series to Game 5
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays were not going to be swept aside by rookie Cooper Pratt and the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays were not going to be swept aside by rookie Cooper Pratt and the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday. Pinch hitter Ben Williamson delivered a walk-off single in the 12th inning as the Rays staved off elimination with a 4-3 victory over the Brewers on Tuesday in Game 4 of the World Series. The Brewers, who squandered a 12th-inning lead, still are up 3-1 in the best-of-seven series. Game 5 is set for Wednesday in St. Petersburg. "Gritty. Gritty. We're dangerous," Tampa Bay's Nick Martinez said. "We have our backs against the wall. ... We know what we have to do. We can win four in a row. This team is capable of doing that." After Pratt capped his four-hit performance with a homer to lead off the top of the 12th, giving Milwaukee a 3-2 lead, Tampa Bay saved its season with an epic rally in the bottom of the inning. Junior Caminero reached on a throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz to open the 12th inning and chase Antonio Senzatela from the game. "There's no excuse. Not one at all," Ortiz said. "I should make that play every f---- time." Shane Drohan (0-1) relieved Senzatela, and allowed a single to Liam Hicks to put runners on the corners. Jonny DeLuca's single up the middle plated pinch runner Cedric Mullins to forge a 3-3 tie. Chandler Simpson's single loaded the bases before Williamson bounced a chopper into right field, knocking in pinch runner Nick Fortes to end the game. Drohan, who was making his first relief appearance since Oct. 15, did not offer any excuses after the game. "(It's) definitely hard. I'm human, but I knew what I was walking into. I just didn't get the job done," said Drohan, who permitted one run on four hits without retiring a batter. Williamson had been 1-for-15 in the postseason before recording the game-winning hit. "You guys know how the game works, it's momentum, and we just got it right now," DeLuca told Fox Sports. "We're going to do everything we can to keep it going into tomorrow, We love the position we're in. We love being underdogs. We know the fight we have in this clubhouse, coaches, team, everyone. It's a fun position to be in." Brewers captain Christian Yelich believes his team will respond from this loss. "You're supposed to face adversity. You have to battle back from it. That's why you celebrate at the end, because that's what it requires out of you," he said. "I believe in our room and I believe we're prepared to meet that challenge." Pratt, who also had an RBI double in the fourth inning, deposited a 2-2 sweeper from Ian Seymour (2-0) over the wall in left-center field in the top of the 12th. Seymour allowed one run on two hits in one inning. Milwaukee's Jackson Chourio recorded two hits, boosting his total to 10 hits in the first four games of a World Series. The only other player to accomplish that feat was Babe Ruth in 1928. The Brewers' David Hamilton atoned for an earlier miscue by homering to lead off the fifth inning, tying the game 2-2. Simpson ripped an RBI double in the second inning and made a leaping catch at the wall in the ninth for the Rays, who (at least temporarily) prevented the Brewers from capturing their first World Series title. In the second, DeLuca reached on a fielder's choice and hustled home on Simpson's double into the right field corner to open the scoring. Sal Frelick reached on a two-out single and scampered home on Pratt's double into the left field corner to forge a 1-1 tie in the fourth inning. Tampa Bay answered in the bottom of the frame. Third baseman Hamilton's throw toward first base sailed off the mark, allowing Caminero to score from second and giving the Rays a 2-1 lead. In the fifth, Hamilton sent a 0-2 fastball from Griffin Jax over the wall in right center field to forge a 2-2 tie. The blast chased Jax from the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: China's CXMT to start advanced AI memory production despite poor yields, sources say
item.description: China's CXMT plans to start production of HBM3E, an advanced type of high-bandwidth memory chip used with AI processors, despite as little as 20% of the chips it makes being usable, two people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's CXMT plans to start production of HBM3E, an advanced type of high-bandwidth memory chip used with AI processors, despite as little as 20% of the chips it makes being usable, two people familiar with the matter said. The decision highlights China's [USN:L1N45902O TEXT:"intense shortage"] of the AI memory chips, which are essential to a government-backed push to develop domestic alternatives to Nvidia's (NVDA.O) AI processors at scale amid US curbs on access to foreign-made technology. ChangXin Memory Technologies (688825.SS) — China's largest maker of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), the conventional memory used in computers and servers — has sent HBM3E samples to several domestic AI chip designers, the people said. It expects to begin limited production over the next two months, one person said. Yields, or the share of chips coming off a production line that meet specifications, are only about 20% to 30%, compared with yields of around 70% at South Korea's SK Hynix (000660.KS) , the market leader, they said. The people declined to be identified because the plans are not public. CXMT did not respond to a request for comment. SK Hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the yield estimate. The Information first reported CXMT's HBM3E plans. Reuters is reporting details about the product yields and delivery timeline for the first time. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) is made by vertically stacking memory chips so they can exchange data rapidly with AI processors. It is a crucial component in the specialized chips used to train and run large language models. Washington tightened export controls on certain advanced HBM products bound for China in December 2024. Chinese chipmakers have increasingly sought the memory through unofficial channels, where it can cost several times more, the people said. CXMT is pressing ahead despite low yields because Chinese AI chipmakers have struggled to obtain enough advanced memory to increase output, the people said. Low yields make production expensive because a large share of chips must be discarded or reworked. Reuters [USN:L1N45102L TEXT:"reported"] last month that Huawei [RIC:RIC:HWT.UL], Cambricon (688256.SS) , MetaX (688802.SS) and Iluvatar CoreX (9903.HK) had raised prices for current and next-generation AI chips by 20% to 50% as memory costs complicated efforts to ramp up production. CXMT's HBM3E is expected to cost more than comparable products from overseas rivals, one of the people said. The company began developing the technology internally as early as 2024, the people added. GENERATIONS BEHIND In testing, CXMT's HBM3E performance was closer to SK Hynix's previous-generation HBM3 than to the South Korean company's HBM3E, one of the people said. CXMT has sent customers two HBM3E versions, the other person said: a standard design and an updated version that includes changes intended to improve yields. The difficulty of producing HBM illustrates the gap between CXMT and the industry's established leaders — SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and Micron Technology (MU.O) — which dominate global supply. SK Hynix held 50% of global HBM revenue in the second quarter, according to Counterpoint Research, followed by Samsung with 33% and Micron with 18%. Most revenue came from HBM3E, the research firm said. CXMT held a 10% share of global DRAM revenue in the quarter, making it the world's fourth-largest supplier of conventional memory chips, Counterpoint said. But US export controls limit its access to some of the most advanced chipmaking equipment, making it harder to close the gap with global rivals. Samsung [USN:P8N41N01J TEXT:"said"] in July that it had expanded HBM4 sales and shipped HBM4E samples to major customers, putting CXMT at least one generation behind in commercial HBM production.

item.title: Boosting Western supply of refined critical metals means de-risking investment. But how?
item.description: The Western world is starting to reel in China's massive lead in producing and controlling the refined metals critical to defence, the transition to cleaner energy and the development of AI-related infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: The Western world is starting to reel in China's massive lead in producing and controlling the refined metals critical to defence, the transition to cleaner energy and the development of AI-related infrastructure. The question is how to translate initial successes into a long-term, economically viable supply chain that bypasses the world's dominant producer. It was this question that dominated the International Mining and Resources Conference (IMARC) this week in Sydney, which brought together miners, governments and financiers to discuss how to turn the resource endowments of countries like [USN:L5N46D0DY TEXT:"Australia"] into refined metals. Unlike China, which can sustain forms of subsidies for state-controlled enterprises for years until economies of scale are achieved, Western nations are shaped more by finance and profitability. But it is also apparent that in a world where China dominates the production of refined metals and prices are often viewed as opaque, the previous model of mine development and downstream processing will not work. The United States is further ahead than the European Union in recognising that if critical minerals and metals are to be obtained in sufficient quantities and via relatively secure supply chains, then government intervention and support are going to be key. The traditional model of junior miners exploring and proving up a resource, then trying to raise capital to build a mine and eventually moving into production simply will not deliver the needed ore when compared with China's subsidy-driven rivals. And even if ore can be successfully mined, refining is often more challenging, especially in countries like Australia, with its high labour and energy costs and stringent environmental approvals. The main question at IMARC was how to significantly move the needle toward more secure supply for Western economies in a world where China controls 99% of the world's refined gallium, 74% of antimony, 81% of molybdenum, 91% of rare earths, 70% of lithium and 44% of copper, showed data from Visual Capitalist. And that is to name just a few of the vital metals. The answers were varied and reflected that no one tactic or policy is likely to deliver the necessary results. But there was some consensus on what measures are likely to bring the greatest chance of more rapid development of mineral resources. DE-RISKING The biggest factor is how to de-risk projects. Under the traditional model financing was only available if the developer could show that the cost of producing the minerals and metals would be less than the expected future price, or that offtake agreements were in place that guaranteed revenue. It was on this basis that Australia was able to approve massive resource expansion, such as Japanese investment into coal and iron ore mines, and both Japanese and Chinese support for liquefied natural gas projects. Australia also jumped in the past decade to become the world's largest lithium producer, but this was achieved largely with Chinese money and the vast majority of the country's mined lithium ore is processed in China for use by Chinese vehicle and battery manufacturers. For more minor metals with opaque pricing the situation is more complex. There are three main tactics to try and speed up development. The first is to set a floor price for the commodity, as the United States has done for the rare earth compound neodymium-praseodymium, which is used to make magnets. The minimum price of $110 per kilogram gives producers certainty and may end up costing US taxpayers nothing as the price of the compound has risen to trade above the floor. The second is to guarantee offtake, giving producers confidence that buyers will be available for the product at prices that will ensure viability, even if those prices are higher than what is charged by Chinese-controlled suppliers. The third is to directly invest in mines and downstream processing and be prepared to subsidise losses until economic viability can be achieved. The trick is in working out which tactic will deliver the best outcome, and this is likely to vary from project to project. For metals where the government is the main buyer, such as those used by defence industries, owning stakes may be the answer. For industries vital to technology and the energy transition, setting minimum prices and ensuring offtake agreements are likely the better solution. What is lacking so far is a comprehensive strategy across the developed Western economies, and at IMARC it was also clear that the United States and the European Union are showing signs of competing with each other, rather than working together. The risk is that the Western response to China's dominance of refined critical metals remains fragmented and uncoordinated. Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI) , your essential new source for global financial commentary. ROI delivers thought-provoking, data-driven analysis of everything from swap rates to soybeans. Markets are moving faster than ever. ROI can help you keep up. Follow ROI on LinkedIn and X . The views expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.

item.title: NBA roundup: Jayson Tatum's OT buzzer-beater lifts Celtics over Nets
item.description: Jayson Tatum made an elbow jumper as time expired in overtime to give the Boston Celtics a 125-124 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jayson Tatum made an elbow jumper as time expired in overtime to give the Boston Celtics a 125-124 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night. Tatum scored a game-high 40 points and hit a career-high 18 free throws on 22 attempts. Paul George added 20 points, seven rebounds and seven assists for Boston, which won its third game in a row. Michael Porter Jr. amassed 27 points and 12 rebounds for the Nets, who fell to 0-4. Julius Randle finished with 24 points and nine rebounds. Brooklyn trailed 117-114 late in the fourth quarter, but Mikel Brown Jr. sent the game to overtime by making a 3-pointer with one second left. Knicks 111, Pistons 97 Karl-Anthony Towns scored 13 of his game-high 27 points during a decisive third-quarter run as host New York rallied past Detroit for its first win of the season. The Knicks outscored the Pistons 37-13 in the third and held off a fourth-quarter rally to avoid becoming the first defending NBA champion to open 0-4 since the Boston Celtics in 1969-70. Towns also pulled down a season-high 20 rebounds, while Jalen Brunson produced 23 points and seven assists. Paul Reed had 22 points and nine rebounds for the Pistons, who were seeking their first 4-0 start since the 2018-19 season. Cade Cunningham totaled 19 points, nine rebounds and eight assists. Spurs 130, Kings 103 Victor Wembanyama poured in 29 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in just 27 minutes, and Julian Champagnie canned eight first-half 3-pointers as host San Antonio steamrolled Sacramento. San Antonio set league season highs for points (80), assists (23) and 3-pointers (13) in a half in a near-complete performance before the break. Champagnie finished with 26 points as the Spurs won their second game in a row. De'Andre Hunter put up 24 points for the Kings, who dropped to 0-4 on the season. Zach LaVine added 22, and Domantas Sabonis amassed 20 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists. --Field Level Media

item.title: Morning Bid: RBNZ throws markets a curveball
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee The shocker in Asia's trading day came from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, which [USN:L6N46E02E TEXT:"unexpectedly left rates on hold"], sending the kiwi sliding. The decision was by a narrow vote and came with agreement that tighter policy is necessary. But according to Westpac, it's the first time outside the pandemic that the central bank held rates while markets had priced a [USN:L2N46E01K TEXT:"more than 70% chance"] of a hike. The New Zealand dollar tumbled more than 1%, and the news sent the Aussie jumping 2% against its Antipodean counterpart to its highest in 13 years. Wednesday's RBNZ decision kicks off a slew of [USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"central bank policy announcements"], with the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Canada set to follow later in the day. The Fed is widely expected to keep rates on hold, while the BoC is [USN:L6N46911N TEXT:"seen hiking"] by 25 basis points, though that could potentially change. If anything, the RBNZ's decision suggests policymakers may be comfortable with playing the waiting game, and that markets may have gotten ahead of themselves in pricing in rate hikes globally. As Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Carol Kong puts it: "Today's decision shows the RBNZ is willing to surprise markets, a reminder that central banks do not take orders from markets." Down Under, [USN:L2N46E00K TEXT:"Australia's inflation"] picked up in the third quarter on higher fuel costs, while stubbornly hot underlying price pressures cemented market expectations of a fifth interest rate hike as soon as next week. South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix (000660.KS) announced [USN:L2N46D1DE TEXT:"shareholder returns"] of about $75 billion on Wednesday, after reporting a more than sevenfold rise in quarterly profit as AI infrastructure continues to drive up memory chip prices. The upbeat results kept [USN:L2N46E012 TEXT:"stocks in Asia"] well supported, with much now riding on earnings from [USN:L3N46D1FP TEXT:"technology giants"] Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) to sustain the momentum. Investors are pressing for evidence that the AI boom can deliver swift returns to justify its enormous price tag. Rising bond yields at AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave (CRWV.O) and record costs to insure Meta Platforms' (META.O) debt have amplified concerns about how the massive AI infrastructure buildout is being funded, particularly as higher US interest rates loom. Meanwhile, Israel's [USN:L2N46D04I TEXT:"wartime election"] appeared deadlocked, exit polls showed, with Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc running neck and neck with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, leaving neither side with a clear path to power. Key developments that could influence markets on Wednesday: - Federal Reserve rate decision - Bank of Canada rate decision - Alphabet, Microsoft earnings

item.title: China dismisses Taiwan's accusations of involvement in comedian attack
item.description: Taiwan is "provoking confrontation" and stirring anti-China sentiment, a Chinese government spokesperson said on Wednesday, after Taiwanese prosecutors indicted five people for plotting to attack a Taiwanese comedian whose shows mocked Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan is "provoking confrontation" and stirring anti-China sentiment, a Chinese government spokesperson said on Wednesday, after Taiwanese prosecutors indicted five people for plotting to attack a Taiwanese [USN:L4N4670DY TEXT:"comedian"] whose shows mocked Beijing. Taiwan, the democratically governed island that China claims as its own territory, has accused Beijing of trying to use "transnational repression" against people in Taiwan the Chinese government views as separatists or politically suspect. Taiwan's government says China was behind last month's attack on comedian Huang Yi-hao, who satirised Chinese President Xi Jinping. Speaking at a regular news conference in Beijing and asked about the incident, Taiwan Affairs Office spokesperson Chen Binhua dismissed Taiwan's accusations as a fabrication by its ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP). "The so-called transnational repression narrative is essentially a way of promoting Taiwan independence and peddling a two-state theory, and it is trotted out every time there is an election on the island," he said, referring to next month's local elections in Taiwan. "The DPP fabricates all kinds of pretexts out of thin air, maliciously smears the mainland, stirs up anti-China sentiment, and provokes cross-strait confrontation, all in an attempt to win political power by misleading the Taiwanese public," Chen said. This is a "tired routine" repeated year after year, he added. Taiwan prosecutors said the defendants, whose full names it has not provided, were paid to fake a car accident and "break the arms and legs" of Huang so he could not perform, though in the end he was only lightly injured. Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung, in a report delivered to lawmakers earlier on Wednesday, said the case of Huang and others showed what he described as China's expanding efforts to "challenge people's personal safety, freedom of expression, and the resilience of democratic society." Other China critics in Taiwan have also been attacked, including [USN:KBN1WE0L8 TEXT:"Hong Kong singer and activist Denise Ho"] in 2019. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the Taiwanese people can decide their future.

item.title: ゆうちょ銀と出資協議を含め提携検討は事実＝一部報道で松井証
item.description: ［東京 ２８日 ロイター］ - 松井証券は２８日、ゆうちょ銀行が松井証の創業家系企業から株を買い取り、２０％ほど出資...

item.content:encoded:
ゆうちょ銀と出資協議を含め提携検討は事実＝一部報道で松井証 13:18 配信

［東京　２８日　ロイター］ - 松井証券は２８日、ゆうちょ銀行が松井証の創業家系企業から株を買い取り、２０％ほど出資する方針を固めたとの日本経済新聞の報道を受け「ゆうちょ銀と出資に関する協議等を含め、提携について検討していることは事実」とのコメントを発表した。

現時点で決定した事実はなく、開示すべき事実が発生した場合は速やかに公表するとしている。

ゆうちょ銀は、中期経営計画で示したコンサルティング事業戦略の中で、松井証を含む証券会社との提携などさまざまな検討をしているとした上で、何ら決定した事実はないとコメントした。

item.title: Unilever India posts higher profit on healthy demand
item.description: Consumer goods maker Hindustan Unilever reported a 6% rise in quarterly profit on Wednesday, as healthy demand cushioned the blow from higher raw material costs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Consumer goods maker Hindustan Unilever (HLL.NS) reported a 6% rise in quarterly profit on Wednesday, as healthy demand cushioned the blow from higher raw material costs. The Indian arm of the UK's Unilever (ULVR.L) , home to brands such as Pepsodent and Dove, said it made a profit of 28.44 billion rupees ($299.01 million) for the quarter ended September 30, compared to 26.9 billion rupees a year earlier. Indian consumer goods makers are seeking to drive growth through wider distribution, more premium products, as well as raising prices to counter higher costs of commodities such as sugar, edible oils and crude oil. For Hindustan Unilever, product sales climbed 15% to 173.99 billion rupees, with volume growing 7% in the quarter through September 30. "Indian economy remains resilient, with healthy macro indicators supporting a positive consumption environment," said CEO and Managing Director Priya Nair. ($1 = 95.1150 Indian rupees)

item.title: StanChart lifts full-year targets after quarterly profit trounces forecasts
item.description: Standard Chartered (StanChart) on Wednesday hiked its income and profitability targets after third-quarter profit handily beat estimates with robust performances from its wealth and global markets divisions.
item.dc:creator: Selena Li, Lawrence White
item.content:encoded: Standard Chartered (StanChart) (STAN.L) on Wednesday hiked its income and profitability targets after third-quarter profit handily beat estimates with robust performances from its wealth and global markets divisions. It lifted its full-year income growth target for 2026 to above 7% from its earlier estimate in the middle of a 5-7% range. And it also boosted its return on tangible equity target, a key performance gauge, to above 14% from an earlier forecast of exceeding 12%. The bank's Hong Kong-listed shares extended gains to be up 5.4% after the results. StanChart, which earns most of its revenue in Asia and Africa, said pretax profit for the July-September quarter surged 27% to $2.25 billion, ahead of a consensus of $1.99 billion drawn from analyst estimates compiled by the bank. Like European peers, StanChart has had a run of strong performances, but its guidance for returns of 14% in 2026 versus the 17% expected by rival HSBC (HSBA.L) shows StanChart still has room to improve. StanChart's wealth division delivered a third consecutive record quarter, with income up 26%, supported by broad-based momentum across products and geographies, the bank said. The bank has accelerated its wealth expansion plan, aiming to gain net new money inflows of $200 billion between 2025 and 2028, ahead of its original 2029 target. Its fee-based revenue, less sensitive to rate changes, surged 19% to $2.81 billion in the quarter from a year earlier, ahead of an average estimate of $2.68 billion.

item.title: JPMorgan to lead US retail offering in Anthropic's potential record IPO
item.description: The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Ryan Gould and Shirin Ghaffary Anthropic PBC has tapped JPMorgan Chase & Co. to lead US sales of shares to individual investors in its potentially record-setting initial public offering, people familiar with the matter said. The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall, some of the people said. JPMorgan Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon is expected to take part in the Wall Street bank’s campaign, one of them added. JPMorgan is reprising its role leading the effort to gather retail orders for SpaceX’s $86.2 billion IPO, which saw more than $100 billion of demand from individual investors, Bloomberg News has reported.  Citigroup Inc. is set to coordinate the international retail offering, some of the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Anthropic’s IPO includes offerings in Australia, Canada, Japan, certain European Economic Area countries, Switzerland and the UK, according to the IPO filing. JPMorgan is coordinating outreach on Anthropic’s IPO to high-net-worth investors and private banking clients as well as broker platforms, the people said. Deliberations are ongoing and details including the share of the offering earmarked for retail could change, the people said. Representatives for Anthropic, JPMorgan and Citigroup declined to comment. Anthropic filed publicly on Monday for an IPO that would see it and some of its investors sell shares, marking the first listing by a company focused primarily on developing the most advanced AI models. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering. Investors are telling bankers on the deal that their estimate of a fair valuation has shifted to around $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion, though a valuation of closer to $1.75 trillion is potentially achievable, Bloomberg News has reported. The amount of money needed to fund the development of AI and its associated infrastructure has spurred companies to raise tens of billions of dollars at a time.  Meta Platforms Inc. on Monday kicked off a plan to raise as much as $98 billion in equity, which would be one of the largest financing exercises of its kind in history. It follows Google parent Alphabet Inc.’s $85 billion equity fundraising plan earlier this year. Anthropic and rival OpenAI are seeking to raise record amounts while facing mounting public scrutiny over AI safety after a string of high-profile hacking incidents by rogue agents.

item.title: France minerals envoy says rare earths diversification from China possible within 3-5 years
item.description: Western countries could achieve an acceptable level of rare earths diversification away from China within three to five years, France's top envoy for strategic metals said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Burton
item.content:encoded: Western countries could achieve an acceptable level of rare earths diversification away from China within three to five years, France's top envoy for strategic metals said on Wednesday. Governments and manufacturers are racing to diversify supplies of metals vital to defence, technology and renewable energy and reduce dependence on China which accounts for as much as 90% of production of some specialised rare earth magnets. Beijing rattled global markets last year when export curbs on permanent magnets disrupted industries, including the automotive sector, exposing their reliance on a single source. Some investors and analysts have questioned whether breaking China's dominance is achievable, given the scale of investment and technical know-how required to produce the niche metals used in everything from cars and aircraft to electronics and weapons systems. "You don't need hundreds of rare earths mines around the world to cover the supply. It's a limited market, it's a limited quantity. We have already made some progress," said Benjamin Gallezot, France's Interministerial Delegate for Strategic Minerals and Metals Supply. Expansion projects led by Belgium's Solvay (SOLB.BR) and France's Carester, plus others in Australia, the US, Japan, Brazil, and India are developing quickly, he said. "If you take all together, these projects, and you push to accelerate them, hopefully you can have a good diversification in the next three to five years," he said, speaking on the sidelines of a mining conference in Sydney. While rare earths mines and refining projects were progressing, the amount of magnet manufacturing could still be a limiting factor, he said. "You don't need a decade to solve this problem." Leaders of the Group of Seven nations agreed in June to step up [USN:L6N42P0XG TEXT:"coordination"] to cut their countries' reliance on China for critical minerals. They aim to reduce dependence on any one supplier outside the G7 and its partner countries for rare earths and permanent magnets to below 60% by 2030, with an ultimate goal of 50% "as soon as possible". "We can do much more," Gallezot said.

item.title: China's aluminium producers push abroad as domestic growth hits ceiling
item.description: Chinese aluminium producers are pushing abroad as part of an expansion spree that could tip the world market for the metal into surplus even as the wave of investment faces greater scrutiny from Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Duan, Lewis Jackson
item.content:encoded: Chinese aluminium producers are pushing abroad as part of an expansion spree that could tip the world market for the metal into surplus even as the wave of investment faces greater scrutiny from Beijing. At least 15 million metric tons a year of primary aluminium smelting capacity is planned or has been announced by Chinese investors across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa, a Reuters review of company disclosures and government filings showed. About 2.85 million tons a year of that is ramping up or under construction, the review showed, equal to 3.8% of current global annual capacity of 73.78 million tons. The new near-term smelter projects, along with recovering Middle East output, will help swing the global aluminium market from a 1.1 million-ton deficit this year to an 830,000-ton surplus next year and a 1.8-million-ton surplus in 2028, Morgan Stanley (MS.N) [USN:L4N43B0SU TEXT:"forecast"] in July. Chinese aluminium producers are looking overseas for growth because domestic smelting capacity is capped at 45 million tons a year under a policy introduced in 2017 to curb overcapacity and pollution. How much of the planned capacity will ultimately be built is unclear, as new supply could lower prices and put projects further down the pipeline at risk. Also, Beijing is increasing its scrutiny of outbound direct investments by Chinese companies and access to power overseas remains an impediment to new plants. "Ultimately, it comes down to economics. Most of these companies are privately owned and profit-driven," said Rachel Zhang, head of China materials research at Morgan Stanley. "If a project clearly does not make money, why would they invest in it?" The expected additions should weigh on metal prices. Morgan Stanley has cut its average price forecast in 2027 to $2,850 a ton and for 2028 to $2,800. It expects aluminium to average $3,150 in the second half of 2026. Benchmark three-month aluminium prices on the London Metal Exchange were at $3,097.50 a ton as of 0300 GMT on Wednesday. Chinese metal demand for manufacturing and electric vehicles that exceeds the domestic capacity cap is driving the overseas expansion as well as the companies' outlook for rising consumption as much as 20 years ahead, said Andrew Denton, research director at metals industry analytics company AME Group in Sydney. "These projects would have to be predicated on a much longer-term view of demand growth for primary aluminium, which we see," he said. "The broader themes for demand with electrification and EVs for aluminium are positive." INDONESIA FIRST Indonesia, which has attracted tens of billions of dollars in Chinese nickel investment, has emerged as a major destination for Chinese aluminium investment. Zhang at Morgan Stanley expects Indonesia to add 866,000 tons of annual smelting capacity in 2026 and another 1.2 million to 1.3 million tons in 2027. The projects include Shandong Nanshan Aluminium's 250,000-ton-per-year facility on the island of Bintan that is under construction, with an expansion that would double capacity planned as well. In Central Sulawesi's Morowali Industrial Park, Xinfa Group and Tsingshan Holding Group are commissioning a facility with a capacity of 600,000 tons per year. Tsingshan is also working on a new facility at the existing smelting hub of Weda Bay in North Maluku province of 800,000 tons per year. Beyond Indonesia, Chinese projects in Kazakhstan and Saudi Arabia would add around 4 million tons a year of capacity. In Saudi Arabia, Shandong Innovation Group-backed Red Sea Aluminium is building a 500,000-ton-a-year smelter in Yanbu, targeting production in 2027. The project reached preliminary partnership terms with the kingdom's Public Investment Fund in January. In Kazakhstan, Xinfa is pursuing a 2.4-million-ton-a-year smelter in Pavlodar, among the largest projects in the pipeline. Globally, Morgan Stanley expects around 2.1 million tons of new annual capacity in 2027 and 2.2 million tons in 2028. SCRUTINY IN BEIJING Still, global prices and Chinese oversight will decide how much is built. Overseas aluminium deals face stricter regulatory scrutiny under [USN:P8N40T00Z TEXT:"new outbound investment rules"] that started in July, according to two sources briefed by some of the Chinese companies that are moving overseas. The rules allow authorities to review overseas investments on national security grounds and order companies to halt projects or divest assets. In October, Fan Shunke, the deputy party secretary of the state-backed China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association, said a huge expansion overseas was not desirable nor feasible. While large integrated projects are still likely to go ahead, though with more delays, the new rules will make it more difficult for smaller stand-alone smelters, according to Alan Clark, Adelaide-based founder of aluminium consultancy CM Group, who has spent more than two decades researching China's metals industry. Of the 15 million tons of new capacity identified by Reuters, Clark estimates that only between 9 million and 10 million tons will eventually be built, about half of that in Indonesia.

item.title: AI worries expose dollar's hot-money problem
item.description: Investors have long treated the US dollar as a refuge when markets fall, but foreign money chasing returns from the AI boom could weaken that safe-haven role if the trade unwinds.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: Investors have long treated the US dollar as a refuge when markets fall, but foreign money chasing returns from the AI boom could weaken that safe-haven role if the trade unwinds. Foreign capital has poured in to US mega-cap equities, hyperscaler corporate bonds and power-grid infrastructure. That has made the dollar an increasingly crowded bet on American exceptionalism, backed by faster growth, higher yields and persistent foreign demand for US assets. But if the AI narrative stumbles, the dollar's safe-haven status could collide with its growing role as a risk-sensitive asset owned increasingly by price-sensitive investors. A sustained selloff in stocks could lead investors to sell US assets, potentially drowning out the safe-haven demand for the currency. If the AI trade unwinds, "it's not as clear the dollar benefits in the same way it would have done in the past," said Dominic Bunning, head of G10 FX strategy at Nomura. STORM WARNING ON FOREX FLOWS Last week [USN:L6N4681D7 TEXT:"offered an early warning"]. When AI valuations came under pressure, haven flows favored the Japanese yen and Swiss franc over the dollar. The greenback managed to eke out modest gains against the euro, mainly due to the single currency being dented by concerns over French civil unrest. "The relationship between the AI trade and the dollar has become much more visible when the AI trade comes under scrutiny," said Kevin Ford, lead FX and macro strategist at Convera. Foreign flows into US equities are at a record, while foreign direct investment has lagged. As a result, much of the capital is coming from institutional allocators that may buy or sell when they reassess US growth, rates, or tech valuations. Erik Nelson, global head of FX strategy at Wells Fargo, likens these allocations to the "hot money" flows that dominate emerging markets. The AI boom has reinforced expectations of stronger US growth, firmer inflation and higher rates, lifting the dollar alongside Treasury yields, analysts said. "The whole AI trade caused US rates to reprice higher, which has caused the dollar to rally," said Noah Buffam, FX strategist at CIBC Capital Markets. If returns disappoint, an unwind could hit equities, credit and rates, leaving the dollar vulnerable on three fronts. Weaker growth could force the Federal Reserve to cut rates, eroding the dollar's yield advantage. Slower domestic investment would puncture the exceptionalism narrative. And fading institutional demand for US corporate bonds and equities would weaken a major source of structural support. So far, investors have been willing to buy dips, suggesting that any sustained weakness could be a process taking months or years. THE DOTCOM LESSON An equity rout alone would not automatically sink the dollar, Nelson said. After the Nasdaq peaked in March 2000, the dollar stayed firm for nearly two years before cracking when US credit markets came under stress following collapses such as WorldCom's, and due to other factors such as a recovery in global growth. But the AI buildout is more US-centric. Nelson said the real trade-weighted dollar has stayed above its long-run average, measured since 1973, for 12 consecutive years, the longest stretch on record. Foreign inflows are also more concentrated in equities and corporate bonds than in 2000, while foreign direct investment is weaker. If infrastructure investments fail to pay off, credit spreads could widen, forcing AI companies to curb capital spending. That could ripple through the economy, softening demand for industrial equipment, hardware and energy. Concerns about riskier parts of the AI universe, such as heavily indebted neocloud companies [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"including CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) , have already widened credit default swap spreads sharply in recent weeks, adding to pressure on stocks. "We can see this fraying around the edges when we look at credit default swaps," said Shaun Osborne, chief FX strategist at Scotiabank. Washington also runs a large fiscal deficit now, compared with a surplus near the 2000 tech peak. That leaves less room for counter-cyclical stimulus without unsettling debt markets. SENSITIVITY UNDER STRESS For Nelson, the key signal is not simply whether US tech shares fall, but whether stress becomes a US-specific credit and growth problem that can also change expectations for Fed policy. In such a scenario the yen would likely benefit at the dollar's expense, a shift that could have further ramifications for markets that would already likely be under stress. That is not to say a dollar decline is a foregone conclusion. A shock severe enough to trigger a scramble for dollar funding could initially strengthen the dollar. In 2008 and March 2020, investors rushed to obtain dollars to meet dollar-denominated liabilities, creating a powerful but temporary bid. In any case, some investors believe the dollar is back on the table as a major risk factor in the most significant way since the rout caused by US President Donald Trump 's announcement of sweeping tariffs in April 2025. "The sensitivity of global investors to a large re-rating or selloff in the dollar is substantial," Nelson said. "As we go into '27, it's a vulnerability for the dollar that I think is worth watching.”

item.title: India's L&T jumps as quarterly profit beat eases Middle East concerns
item.description: Shares of India's Larsen & Toubro rose more than 6% in early trading on Wednesday after the engineering conglomerate posted a 33% jump in second-quarter profit, driven by strong order inflows and easing concerns over Middle East project execution.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of India's Larsen & Toubro rose more than 6% in early trading on Wednesday after the engineering conglomerate posted a 33% jump in second-quarter profit, driven by strong order inflows and easing concerns over Middle East project execution. The stock was up 4.38% at 3,826.10 rupees, as of 9:35 a.m. IST. L&T, seen as a barometer for India's infrastructure sector, [USN:L3N46D162 TEXT:"reported"] a profit of 52.02 billion rupees ($546.92 million) in July-September on Tuesday, while revenue rose 16% to 787.5 billion rupees. Order inflows rose 28% to 1.48 trillion rupees in the reported quarter, taking the company's outstanding order book to a record 8.54 trillion rupees. International orders accounted for 63% of new orders. J.P. Morgan said L&T's strong execution, despite the ongoing Middle East conflict, eased concerns about its ability to meet annual growth targets, noting that projects in the region continued despite logistical challenges. The brokerage maintained its "Overweight" rating but lowered its price target to 4,960 rupees from 5,060 rupees, citing higher logistics costs affecting solar projects in the Middle East. Investec raised its profit estimates for fiscal 2027 through 2029 by 3%-4% on stronger-than-expected revenue growth, healthy order inflows and improved working capital. It maintained its "Buy" rating and raised its price target to 5,000 rupees from 4,870 rupees. Jefferies also maintained its "Buy" rating, citing L&T's strong order book and execution, but cut its price target to 4,700 rupees from 5,000 rupees to account for weaker engineering and construction margins. L&T maintained its fiscal 2027 guidance for revenue and order inflow growth of 10%-12% each, despite geopolitical tensions affecting some projects in the Middle East. ($1 = 95.1150 Indian rupees)

item.title: ウクライナ軍が領土奪還、ゼレンスキー氏演説 「戦況良好」
item.description: ［２７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２７日　ロイター］ - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２７日、ウクライナ軍が一連の攻撃を通じて領土を奪還していると述べた。

夜のビデオ演説で、４年半に及ぶ戦争の中でウクライナ軍の戦況はこのところ最も良好だと指摘。欧米の同盟国から防空システムの供与が増えれば、さらに優位に立てると強調した。

軍幹部の報告を引用し、北東部でパイプラインを利用した「ベレス」作戦に初めて言及。東部での空中強襲作戦や、そのさらに北方で重要地域でのロシア軍の前進を阻止するために実施した「ビバルディ」作戦にも触れた。

ベレス作戦は、北東部ハルキウ州の都市クピャンスク近郊で実施したという。同市はウクライナ軍が２０２２年終盤に奪還したが、その後もロシア軍の圧力に絶えずさらされている。

ゼレンスキー氏は「綿密に計画され、技術を駆使した強力な作戦だ。ロシア軍は地下のガスパイプラインを使って、われわれの陣地を迂回して前進しようとした」と説明。「われわれの兵士はこの戦術を逆手に取り、地下インフラを占領者に対して利用して、極めて大きな成果を上げた」と語った。

item.title: India's Bajaj Auto gains as export strength, EV growth drive earnings beat
item.description: Shares of India's Bajaj Auto rose as much as 3.1% on Wednesday after the motorcycle maker's quarterly profit beat estimates, reinforcing expectations that strong export demand and rapid growth in its electric-vehicle business will drive its next phase of expansion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of India's Bajaj Auto (BAJA.NS) rose as much as 3.1% on Wednesday after the motorcycle maker's quarterly profit beat estimates, reinforcing expectations that strong export demand and rapid growth in its electric-vehicle business will drive its next phase of expansion. The stock was up 2% at 10,600 rupees as of 10:17 a.m. IST. The Nifty Auto index was up 0.3%, while the benchmark Nifty 50 index was down 1%. Bajaj, which makes the Pulsar motorcycles and electric Chetak two-wheeler, reported a 35.3% rise in second-quarter profit while revenue from operations rose 34.1%. Export volumes jumped 41%, outpacing growth in its domestic two-wheeler business. Exports and EVs are emerging as Bajaj Auto's twin growth engines, helping offset cost pressures and boost investor confidence in its earnings momentum, analysts said. The company said its EV business accounted for nearly 35% of domestic revenue in the quarter. It plans to raise monthly Chetak production capacity to about 80,000 units by the fourth quarter from 60,000-65,000 currently. Citi said sustained export momentum and festive demand supported its growth outlook, while CLSA said higher Chetak capacity, refreshed Pulsar models and two planned motorcycle brands could help Bajaj gain market share. CLSA retained its "outperform" rating and raised its fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings estimates by 4%. Analysts also highlighted strong realisations from favourable currency movements. Morgan Stanley said the company's EBITDA margin beat its estimates, aided by foreign-exchange gains, production-linked incentives and a more favourable export mix. EV capacity additions and planned launches supported the growth outlook, it added, but retained its "underweight" rating, citing risks to sustaining current margins amid elevated commodity costs.

item.title: 中国外務省、エムバペの「独裁者」発言を批判 「国民感情を傷つける発言には各界から反発」
item.description:

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国外務省の郭嘉昆報道官は27日の定例記者会見で、サッカーのフランス代表主将、キリアン・エムバペ選手が中国の故毛沢東主席を「独裁者」と呼んだとみられる発言について問われ、中国国民の感情を傷つける言動は「当然、中国社会の各界から一致した反発を受けることになる」と述べた。

郭報道官は定例記者会見で、中国政府は「関連報道を承知している」と述べた。

26日にインターネット上に出回った動画では、エムバペ選手が、自分を題材にしたミーム（ネット上で拡散されるパロディー画像など）の中で最も面白かったのは、「中国の独裁者」の顔を自分の顔に置き換えたものだと話す様子が収められている。騒動の背景には、ファンがエムバペ選手の所属チームでの影響力を皮肉り、軍事や政治の指導者の画像に同選手の顔を重ねたミームを作っていることがある。ロイターはこの動画の真偽を確認できていない。

エムバペ選手は27日、自身のコメントについて謝罪。声明で「私の発言は軽率だった。中国や世界各地の中国人コミュニティーの多くの人々を傷つけたことを、今は理解している」とし、「私の言葉で不快な思いをした全ての方々に謝罪する。決してそのような意図はなかった」と表明した。

中国では毛沢東をジョークの題材にすることは今も社会的なタブーとなっている。この問題を受け、乳製品メーカーの蒙牛乳業と上海妙可藍多食品科技、飲料メーカーの東鵬飲料などは、エムバペ選手との全ての提携関係を即時終了すると発表した。また政府系メディアによると、中国国営テレビはスペイン1部とエムバペ選手に関連する全ての試合やイベントの放送を停止し、同選手が登場する広告も全て撤去された。

item.title: 米軍、東太平洋で船舶攻撃 5人死亡 「麻薬テロリスト」標的と主張
item.description:
［ワシントン ２７日 ロイター］ - 米軍は２７日、東太平洋で船舶を攻撃し、５人が死亡したと発表した。米政府が「麻薬テロリスト」を標的としていると主張する一連の攻撃の最新事例となるが、人権専門家はこうした攻撃を超法規的殺害だと非難している。
• 米南方軍はＸへの投稿で、「東太平洋の既知の麻薬密輸ルートを航行する高速艇に対し、殺傷力を伴う武力攻撃を実施した」と明らかにした。
• 「確認済みの情報」に基づき、船舶が麻薬密輸に積極的に関与していたと主張したが、詳しい説明はしなかった。「麻薬テロリスト」の５人が死亡したとした。
• トランプ米政権は、２０２５年９月以降に攻撃した船舶について、麻薬を輸送していたと主張。米軍がカリブ海と東太平洋で実施したこうした船舶への攻撃で２３０人以上が死亡している。
•

• 「確認済みの情報」に基づき、船舶が麻薬密輸に積極的に関与していたと主張したが、詳しい説明はしなかった。「麻薬テロリスト」の５人が死亡したとした。
