Visa's extensive digital payments network, which spans more than 200 countries and territories, positions it to better endure economic downturns as billions of people globally rely on the card network for everyday spending and other purchases. CLIENT INCENTIVES, PROFIT FORECAST IN FOCUS Client incentives jumped 21 per cent to $5.1 billion in the quarter from the prior year, largely driven by new deals that were signed during the July to September period and early in the fourth quarter. "The one thing to nitpick is client incentives, which were above expectations," Seaport analyst Jeff Cantwell said, adding the development likely impacted Visa's fiscal 2027 forecasts. Suh told analysts incentives growth would step up in fiscal 2027 as Visa is expecting around 25 per cent of its payments volumes to be renewed, including with several large clients. That compares with 20 per cent in fiscal 2026. The company anticipates fiscal 2027 profit per share growth between a low-double-digit and low-teens percentage, while net revenue growth is expected to be in the low-double-digit percentage. "While some may be underwhelmed by the EPS guide, we think it likely reflects... (the management's) decision to keep investing in long-term strategic initiatives to extend the durability of top-line growth," KBW analysts led by Sanjay Sakhrani said. Visa's shares fell about 1.4 per cent in extended trading. The stock has gained 14.6 per cent this year through the last close. On an adjusted basis, it earned $3.48 per share in the three months ended September 30, beating an expectation of $3.44 per share, according to estimates compiled by LSEG. CROSS-BORDER STRENGTH Cross-border volumes excluding intra-Europe, a measure of international travel demand, were a bright spot as they jumped 14 per cent in the quarter on a constant-dollar basis. "It is reflective of strong consumer sentiment, strong demand for travel experiences, and the fact that e-commerce has also just expanded," Suh said. Suh told Reuters travel in and out of the Middle East was also coming back closer to normal levels after being suppressed due to the Iran conflict. The FIFA World Cup, which ran from June 11 to July 19, has also helped boost activity across Visa's network as it brought many visitors to the United States. "XB (cross-border) showed a nice step-up in growth sequentially, and that was one area we were watching for signs of potential weakness going into earnings," Seaport's Cantwell said. Net revenue jumped 13 per cent to $12.1 billion in the quarter. For fiscal year 2026, Visa hauled record net revenue of $46 billion. Rival Mastercard is set to report quarterly earnings later this week.

Source: Reuters

Logitech beats profit forecast as sales of gaming, conferencing products rise

ZURICH, Oct 27 : Logitech International on Tuesday reported a better-than-expected profit for the second quarter, with the computer mouse and keyboard maker seeing higher demand for its gaming and video conferencing devices. The Swiss-U.S. company reported non-GAAP operating income of $231 million for the three months to the end of September, beating forecasts for $204 million in a consensus gathered by Visible Alpha and the company's own guidance for $185 million to $210 million. Sales rose 3 per cent to $1.22 billion, in line with analyst forecasts and towards the upper end of the company's own outlook of $1.19 billion to $1.22 billion. CEO Hanneke Faber said Logitech had come through a difficult period marked by tight component sourcing, higher costs and the conflict in the Middle East.

"Even as global PC shipments declined by 20 per cent in the quarter, our pointing devices and keyboards grew by mid single digits, demonstrating our growth opportunity comes from the large installed PC base," she told analysts on a call. Innovation, including products like matcha and latte-coloured mice, had helped the company grow sales in that category, while 15 new products in the gaming category boosted sales there. Sales of video collaboration equipment rose 12 per cent as business customers refreshed their workplaces after encouraging staff back to the office. "Video collaboration demand is strong and we expect it to continue to be strong," Faber said. "It's not discretionary. You need to refresh those rooms, you need expanded office space if you are going to ask people to come back to work." Faber said there was strong demand from healthcare and government customers. Logitech also said it had suffered a lower-than-expected impact from the forced closure at a factory of one of its semiconductor suppliers at the end of June, which it originally expected to cost it up to $200 million in lost sales in the next quarter. After getting chips from other suppliers, the company said it now expects the impact to be $70 million to $80 million. Logitech said its sales would be in the range of $1.36 billion to $1.43 billion for the three months to the end of December. It also expects non-GAAP operating income of $220 million to $255 million down from $312 million a year earlier, due to higher component and transport costs, as well as the lost sales caused by the factory shutdown.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 米国株式市場＝続伸、ＡＩ関連のハイテク株高がけん引
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ２７日 ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は続伸して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連のハイテク株が買われた。...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝続伸、ＡＩ関連のハイテク株高がけん引 5:09 配信

2023年2月17日に撮影。REUTERS/Florence Lo/Illustration/File Photo（ロイター） ［ニューヨーク　２７日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は続伸して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連のハイテク株が買われた。ハイテク株の比重が高いナスダック総合が上昇率で主要指数をリードした。

ＡＩ開発の米アンソロピックが近く実施する新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）の詳細を巡る期待感から、半導体株指数は３営業日続伸した。

借り入れコストが上昇する中、債務で賄う支出の持続性を巡る懸念が強まり、今月はＡＩ関連取引の重しとなっていた。フィラデルフィア半導体指数は６月２２日に付けた終値での過去最高値から２０％超下落しているものの、年初来では６２．１％上昇し、同期間に１２．８％上昇したＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種を上回っている。

メタ・プラットフォームズはＡＩ事業拡大の資金を確保するため、同社として過去最大となる株式発行による資金調達額を９７５億ドルに引き上げたと発表。株価は１．６％下落した。

ホライズン・インベストメント・サービシズのチャック・カールソン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「（アンソロピックのニュースが）ＡＩ関連株、特に半導体株に幾分、リリーフラリー（安心感からの上昇）をもたらしているようだ」とし、「これらの銘柄はここ数週間で大きく売り込まれており、おそらく反発する頃合いだった」と述べた。

航空機大手ボーイングは１０．７％急落。７─９月期の調整後損益が予想より大幅な赤字となった。

四半期利益が予想を下回ったシャーウィン・ウィリアムズも２．７％下落し、ダウ工業株３０種の重しとなった。

一方、ユナイテッド・パーセル・サービス（ＵＰＳ）は５．８％上昇。通期の売上高と利益の見通し引き上げを好感した。

クルーズ船運航のロイヤル・カリビアンも通期利益見通しを引き上げ、５．５％高となった。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１セクターでは情報技術が上昇率トップだった。一方、中東の和平交渉に関心が向かい、原油価格が下落したことで、エネルギーの下落率が最大となった。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値上がり銘柄数が値下がり銘柄数を１．８３対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも１．８６対１で値上がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は約１６１億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７１億８０００万株。

item.title: ボーイング株急落、７３７生産遅れやＦＣＦ見通し下方修正で
item.description:
Dan Catchpole Shivansh Tiwary
[シアトル ２７日 ロイター] - 米航空機大手ボーイング...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ボーイング株急落、７３７生産遅れやＦＣＦ見通し下方修正で 5:08 配信

2026年10月20日、米国ワシントン州エベレットで撮影。REUTERS/Jason Redmond（ロイター） Dan Catchpole　Shivansh Tiwary

[シアトル ２７日 ロイター] - 米航空機大手ボーイングが２７日発表した７─９月期決算は、調整後損益が１株当たり０．３４ドルの赤字と、ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想の０．２１ドルの赤字を上回る赤字幅となった。また、フリーキャッシュフロー（ＦＣＦ、純現金収支）の伸びがアナリスト予想を下回り、１００億ドルの目標達成は市場予想より１年遅い２０２９年になるとの見通しを示した。

さらにケリー・オートバーグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、主力旅客機である７３７について、今年の生産目標と航空機の納入目標を達成できないとの見通しを示した。

株価は午後の取引で１０％超下落。２０２５年４月以来の大幅安となった。

ボーイングは同四半期にＦＣＦ４億６４００万ドルを計上した。今年これまでに３億５９００万ドルのキャッシュを費消したが、なお年末までに２０億ドルを創出する見込みだとしている。

ジェフリーズのアナリスト、シーラ・カヤオグル氏は２７日の調査リポートで、ボーイングは来年３０億ドルを創出する見込みだが、納入減と設備投資増により、市場予想である５５億ドルを下回ると指摘した。

ゲイベリ・ファンズの投資アナリスト、トニー・ゲイベリ氏によると、航空機需要が高く、主要な競合が欧州のエアバス１社のみであることから、ボーイングの長期見通しは依然良好だが、それでも投資家は売りに傾きやすくなる可能性がある。同氏は、キャッシュフロー改善の遅れはいかなるものでも市場に嫌気されるだろうと述べた。

＜生産の苦戦＞

ボーイングは現在、７３７の月産４７機という生産目標の達成時期を２０２７年初めと見込んでいる。同社幹部は５月の時点では、今年の夏にこのペースに達するとしていた。

ジェイ・マレーブ最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）によると、この結果、ボーイングは今年、５００機の納入目標を達成できない見通し。

オートバーグＣＥＯは、主翼の生産が引き続き主要な制約要因となっているものの、ボーイングはなお２０２７年下半期に月産５２機への引き上げを計画していると述べた。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 10/28(水) 5:08 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: UPS CEO sees $15 billion annual revenue opportunity from data center boom
item.description: LOS ANGELES, Oct 27 : UPS CEO Carol Tome told Reuters on Tuesday the AI data center boom is a decades-long opportunity for the world's largest parcel delivery and logistics company, which aims to boost profits by handling fewer, but more premium, shipments. Global data center spending is estimated to hit

UPS CEO sees $15 billion annual revenue opportunity from data center boom

FAST

LOS ANGELES, Oct 27 : UPS CEO Carol Tome told Reuters on Tuesday the AI data center boom is a decades-long opportunity for the world's largest parcel delivery and logistics company, which aims to boost profits by handling fewer, but more premium, shipments.   Global data center spending is estimated to hit roughly $1 trillion in 2026 and more than double before the end of the decade as tech giants like Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon invest billions of dollars in artificial intelligence facilities, which require significant new electricity infrastructure to power and cool servers and computer chips.  The logistics opportunity associated with data centers is $15 billion per year, said Tome.  "It is from manufacturing floor to front door," she said. UPS is flying in critical components such as advanced microprocessors, arranging ocean shipments for equipment of all shapes and sizes, warehousing goods and delivering parts to project sites.

Tome spoke after UPS raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. Data center projects have become divisive as communities weigh job creation and economic growth against electricity prices, water use and noise. Investors separately are questioning companies' massive investments in them. Nevertheless, there are many projects underway and once those are built, there will continue to be demand for parts and equipment to keep them running, Tome said. "This is something that's going to be decades," Tome said of demand. While UPS data center revenue is growing quickly, it has not yet matched revenue from its healthcare segment, which hit $3 billion in the latest quarter, Tome said, declining to give a figure for the newer business. INFLECTION POINT As part of Tome's "better, not bigger" growth strategy, UPS has been reconfiguring its network to be smaller, nimbler and more profitable.  It has consolidated facilities to reduce costs and improved service quality by investing in things like temperature sensors as well as package scanning and tracking. It also has focused on high-growth and high-margin segments like healthcare, returns and, most recently, data centers.   UPS has made significant headway in specialized healthcare logistics, shipping temperature-controlled chemotherapy drugs, cancer treatments and direct-to-consumer GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. It is now the largest player in the $148 billion global healthcare market after some key acquisitions and internal growth.    That business generated revenue of $6 billion for UPS in 2020 and is forecast to reach $13 billion in revenue this year, Tome said.   UPS is racing rival FedEx for the same high-margin volume as they each wean off low-margin to unprofitable deliveries of online purchases and other goods. FedEx, which has set up a dedicated team to court data center-related business, will report quarterly results after the market close on Wednesday. Meanwhile, retailers like Amazon.com  and Walmart as well as growing rivals like OnTrac are aggressively targeting domestic shipments in certain parts of the country. Some of that includes volume UPS and FedEx don't want.  UPS has cut doorstep deliveries of millions of packages for Amazon that it considered unprofitable, which helped lift its margin. Tome said the margin would keep improving every year. "We've moved through an important inflection point," Tome said.

Source: Reuters

まちまちで取引を終えた。英政府の予算案発表を２８日に控え、投資家には様子見姿勢も目立った。ＦＴ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（27日） 3:56 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

まちまちで取引を終えた。英政府の予算案発表を２８日に控え、投資家には様子見姿勢も目立った。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反落。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．８８％高と続伸した。

金融大手ＨＳＢＣは５．４％安。資産運用事業の伸び鈍化などで、２０２６年７─９月期の収益が市場予想を下回り、売られた。ナットウエストは１．５％、ロイズは０．３％それぞれ下落。一方、バークレイズは０．８％上昇した。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種生活必需品株指数は１．２６％安。通期予想への懸念から日用品のレキット・ベンキーザーは４．９％下落した。

イベント主催会社のインフォーマは２．４％高。スタイフェルが目標株価を引き上げたテクノロジー・サービスプロバイダーのコンピュータセンターは１．２％上昇した。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。企業決算での堅調な業績や、原油先物価格の上昇一服が好材料視された。下落が目立っていたフランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は０．５１％高だった。

米アンソロピックの新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）申請の動きを受け、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種テクノロジー株指数は１．９９％高。オランダの半導体組立装置メーカー、ＢＥセミコンダクターは１１．４％高。米半導体製造装置大手アプライド・マテリアルズによる出資の引き上げを受け、買われた。

直近決算の売上高が市場予想を上回ったスイスの容器メーカー、ＳＩＧグループは９．６％上昇した。

資源株指数は２．０８％高。

通期業績見通しを引き上げたスイスの製薬大手ノバルティスは１．０％上昇。

一方、金融大手ＨＳＢＣは５．４％安。２０２６年７─９月期決算の収入が市場予想を下回り、売られた。

フランスの１０月の消費者信頼感指数は１３年６月以来の低水準となった。市場では、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が２９日に開く金融政策決定会合で、政策金利を据え置くとの観測が根強い。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが総じて低下し、フランス国債利回りは落ち着いた動きとなった。中東和平協議が進展する可能性に市場の関心が再び向かい、原油価格が下落したことが背景。

フランス１０年国債利回りは、終盤で４．９１％と横ばい。２３日に格付け会社ムーディーズによる格下げを回避したことを受け、２６日には約１１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下し、１日の低下幅として５カ月ぶりの大きさとなった。この動きを受けて利益確定売りが出たため、２７日序盤には利回りが上昇していた。

コロンビア・スレッドニードのシニアエコノミスト、アンソニー・ウィリス氏は「政治的な決着や予算合意が直ちに実現する見込みはほとんどない。議会審議は今後数週間続く見通しで、フランスの財政政策は引き続き市場の緊張要因となりそうだ」と述べた。

安全資産であり、ユーロ圏国債市場全体の指標となるドイツ１０年国債利回りは１．１ｂｐ低下の３．３４％。同２年国債利回りは４．３ｂｐ低下の３．０３６％となった。

ベルギー国債も同国の重い債務負担を背景に、このところ売り圧力にさらされている。ベルギー１０年国債利回りは２７日、１ｂｐ強上昇して４．４％となった。ただ、上昇幅はフランス国債よりはるかに小さい。

item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 27 : The US Federal Election Commission's website was targeted by a hacker or hackers, according to an email seen by Reuters, disrupting the agency's electronic filings system a week before the November 3 elections.The hack comes as so-called super PACs and dark money groups spend record sums in

item.content:encoded:

Exclusive-Hackers target US FEC system, disrupting campaign finance disclosures days before midterms

The offices of the Federal Election Commission are seen in Washington, D.C., U.S., May 11, 2021. REUTERS/Andrew Kelly

A 3D printed model of men working on computers are seen in front of displayed binary code and words "Hacker" in this illustration taken, July 5, 2021. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 27 : The US Federal Election Commission's website was targeted by a hacker or hackers, according to an email seen by Reuters, disrupting the agency's electronic filings system a week before the November 3 elections. The hack comes as so-called super PACs and dark money groups spend record sums in the final days of the races. The elections will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republicans maintain their majorities in Congress for the next two years.  In a statement, the FEC said, "At this time, the FEC's electronic filing system is currently offline and our IT staff are actively working to restore service." The FEC, which tracks the spending of candidates and political committees, said users could still search the website for past reports. A status message posted by the FEC said its filing system had been down since around 10 p.m. ET on Monday (0200 GMT Tuesday). Around 8 p.m. ET on Tuesday (0000 GMT Wednesday), a new status message said the issue "has been identified and a fix is being implemented." The FEC did not immediately return a message seeking comment and a notice on its website said its filing system remained offline.

The FEC does not play a role in administering US elections and the outage should have no effect on voters' ability to cast ballots. The outage does prevent organizations from filing the FEC's 24-hour and 48-hour spending reports, which show how much political groups and others are spending on specific races. "I've never seen this in 26 years," said Steven Mele, president and CEO at political finance compliance firm MBA Consulting Group. The FEC posted the notice to its website after campaign finance officers could not file mandatory reports late on Monday.  "We have a bad actor attempting to breach FEC systems. As a result, we’ve had to temporarily shut down our web facing services," an FEC electronic filings officer said in the email to several campaign compliance firms that night.  The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the FBI both referred questions to the FEC.  The midterms are now the most expensive US election in history with roughly $11.21 billion spent on advertising and future reservations so far, according to political ad tracker AdImpact. They have surpassed the previous record set in the 2024 elections when $11.2 billion was spent on all races, including $3.2 billion on the presidential race between Trump and former Vice President Kamala Harris, AdImpact said.  Much of the spending is being driven by super PACs, which can accept unlimited amounts of money from wealthy individuals and corporations and spend as much as they want on campaigns with few restrictions.  The sums being spent in recent weeks are staggering as Democrats gain ground in several Republican strongholds. Super PACs and dark money groups have spent an average of over $50 million per day over the last week, said Brendan Glavin, research director at nonpartisan campaign watchdog group OpenSecrets. More than $250 million in spending was reported on October 20 alone, he added.  "It's a big deal," he said of the outage, which leaves voters in the dark until the filing system is back online.  "These are the key reports that tell us what is happening," Glavin said. "In the last days of the election this is the only way for us to keep track of where the money's being spent" and who's spending it.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Food and household brands warn of more price hikes as Iran war costs bite
item.description: The world's top consumer goods and food companies, from Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble to Nestle and Reckitt, have warned of further price hikes next year to cover rising costs even as shoppers remain reluctant to splurge on groceries.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Marrow, Anuja Mistry
item.content:encoded: The world's top consumer goods and food companies, from Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble to Nestle and Reckitt, have warned of further price hikes next year to cover rising costs even as shoppers remain reluctant to splurge on groceries. Higher energy, raw material and freight costs as a result of the US war on Iran mean that the companies making everything from laundry detergent to soda and snacks face a balancing act to protect profit margins. Even higher prices on everyday items will fuel concerns that inflation will persist into next year. High gas and grocery bills are a big factor in next week's US midterm elections . Soaring costs related to the war are the latest headache for consumer goods, food and drink companies, which have struggled with lacklustre sales since the pandemic, as shoppers have baulked at increasingly expensive name-brand packaged food. Last year, they had to contend with tariffs on imported goods imposed by US President Donald Trump. "Pricing is the last lever these companies have left, and they’re pulling it into a consumer who’s already tapped out on paying more," said David Wagner, head of equity and portfolio manager at PepsiCo investor Aptus Capital Advisors. On Tuesday, Coca-Cola (KO.N) CEO Henrique Braun said pressure on consumers could extend into 2027. "We are seeing elevated cost pressures ... driven by increased logistics and transportation costs," he said as the company [USN:L3N46D109 TEXT:"raised its annual profit forecast"]. HOW HIGH CAN PRICES GO? The challenge is working out how high prices can rise before shoppers walk away. The chair of Lindt & Sprüngli (LISN.S) said the Swiss chocolate maker is struggling because it [USN:L2N46A04K TEXT:"misjudged"] how consumers would respond to price increases. He spoke days after the company [USN:L6N4650EX TEXT:"ousted its CEO"] over concerns about its performance. Companies are running out of ways to absorb costs. Consumers in Europe and North America are particularly squeezed, said Reckitt (RKT.L) CEO Kris Licht. He said companies must decide how much of the cost increase to pass on through pricing and how much to offset with more promotional spending. "We will probably have to price more at this level of commodity costs and input costs," Licht said after the Durex maker trimmed its annual revenue forecast, sending its shares down around 5% on Tuesday. Procter & Gamble (PG.N) CFO Andre Schulten expressed a similar view after the Tide detergent maker last week hiked its expected [USN:L4N46811U TEXT:"hit to profit"] from rising raw material, energy and freight costs to $1.4 billion from $1 billion. "At this level of commodity pressure ... the industry generally is pricing up because there is no way to recover this level of commodity pressure without pricing," Schulten said. Procter & Gamble's pricing and sales held steady in the last quarter, but higher costs really hurt margins, said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management. "Consumers are still spending if they see the value ... but we likely are near the upper limit of what consumers are willing to pay for snacks," Mulberry said. PepsiCo (PEP.O) has swung between price rises and cuts this year in an effort to boost sluggish sales and it [USN:L6N45U0N9 TEXT:"suffered a margin hit"] last quarter. Raising prices risks losing customers. Nestle (NESN.S) CFO Anna Manz said last week that volumes can dip in the short term when the company raises prices, as consumers adjust. "Looking forward, there's now again some upward pressure on input costs," Manz said as Nestle posted faster quarterly volume growth than pricing growth [USN:L6N4680BP TEXT:"for the first time"] since 2024. "We'll take pricing to the extent we can without damaging medium-term consumer penetration," she said.

FAST

Oct 27 : The Federal Communications Commission said on Tuesday it approved Amazon Leo’s $11.5 billion deal to acquire Globalstar as the retail giant's satellite arm seeks to build a communications network to compete with SpaceX's Starlink. Amazon Leo has launched nearly 400 satellites since April 2025 and aims to deploy thousands of satellites in Earth's low orbit by 2029. Through the deal, Amazon adds Globalstar's two dozen satellites and its mobile-satellite spectrum. Amazon, which has committed to investing more than $10 billion in Leo, is preparing to roll out its commercial satellite services by the end of 2026, the FCC said. The FCC said the companies’ assets will boost Amazon Leo’s entry into the direct-to-device market and allow the satellite operator to offer fixed and mobile services. "The FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country," FCC Chair Brendan Carr said.

Tech companies are pouring billions of dollars into capturing the lucrative market for satellite-based connectivity as they race to compete with Starlink's network of more than 11,000 satellites. Amazon praised the approval, saying it "brings us a step closer to bringing new connectivity capabilities to customers." Amazon in July sought approval from the FCC for up to 5,105 satellites. Direct-to-device satellite technology allows smartphones and other devices to connect directly to satellites. The FCC will vote on Thursday to advance a new auction of wireless spectrum to boost "direct-to-device" services. Globalstar currently powers satellite-based safety features such as Emergency SOS and Find My for Apple's iPhone and Apple Watch users. Amazon said earlier that it has signed an agreement with Apple to continue providing those services. Apple invested about $1.5 billion in Globalstar in 2024 to fund the expansion of its iPhone communication services, in a deal that also gave the tech giant a 20 per cent equity stake in Globalstar. Apple accounted for about 63 per cent of Globalstar's revenue last year and Amazon plans to acquire Apple's stake, the FCC said. Globalstar said late last year that a new, Apple-backed network under development would expand its footprint to 54 satellites, including a small number of backups, from the two dozen currently.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Judge skeptical of Justice Dept lawsuit over alleged noncitizens on voting rolls
item.description: A US judge appeared skeptical on Tuesday of the Justice Department's request to block California from counting any mail ballots for the November 3 midterm election from more than 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration alleges are noncitizens.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen, Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: A US judge appeared skeptical on Tuesday of the Justice Department's request to block California from counting any mail ballots for the November 3 midterm election from more than 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration alleges are noncitizens. During a hearing in Los Angeles, US District Judge David Carter said he was concerned the request to sequester ballots could disenfranchise and confuse legitimate voters, calling it a "monumental change" to election procedures when voting was already underway. He said he would issue a ruling on Wednesday on the Justice Department's request for a temporary order barring officials from [USN:L6N46117W TEXT:"counting any ballots"] from the individuals the administration has flagged as noncitizens. The lawsuit marks a rare intervention by the Justice Department in the voting process weeks before the midterms, with Donald Trump's Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress. Several states. including California, have begun early voting. Justice Department lawyer Bilal Essayli said during the hearing the federal government had made a narrow request intended to ensure election integrity. Carter responded that the "traditional remedy" for voter fraud was a criminal indictment, and said unlawfully cast ballots can be removed in the weeks after Election Day, prior to certification of the official results. "You've got a remedy, for goodness sake," the judge told the prosecutor. "Go out and indict." The US Constitution assigns individual states the responsibility of administering elections, though the federal government has some oversight role. California has said the state's safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust. Anne Bellows, a lawyer for California, said during Tuesday's hearing the Justice Department's assertions relied on "mysterious database methods" and that complying with its demands would risk disenfranchising eligible voters. "The Supreme Court has reiterated time and again that, as an election is close at hand, federal courts should not interfere to change the rules under which that election is held," Bellows added. "This applies with even more force when the election is ongoing." California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold. It has more seats in the House of Representatives — 52 — than any other state. Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through its "sanctuary state" policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. Trump has repeatedly insisted that states are not doing enough to stop voting by noncitizens, which he says is widespread despite multiple studies and state audits showing it is rare. The US Justice Department on October 16 [USN:L1N46212B TEXT:"warned"] California election officials they could face criminal liability if they counted ballots from voters the Trump administration had flagged as potential noncitizens. "This court believes that it would be wise that any threats to state and county election employees cease immediately," Carter told government lawyers during Tuesday's hearing. ADDITIONAL TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ACTIONS The hearing came after a federal appeals court on Monday [USN:L2N46C163 TEXT:"rejected"] an unusual emergency request by the Justice Department asking the appeals court to temporarily block California from counting the ballots before Carter had the chance to rule. The Justice Department did not indicate how many of the more than 20,000 people it flagged in California had actually submitted a mail ballot. Apart from California, the Trump administration has sought to intervene in elections in two states that are home to [USN:L6N4670ZS TEXT:"competitive races"]. In Alaska, the Justice Department last week asked a judge to [USN:L2N46D019 TEXT:"prevent certification"] of election results if the Republican incumbent senator loses by a slim margin, alleging the presence of another candidate with a similar name on the ballot could confuse voters. Alaska has urged that the case be dismissed, arguing it has taken steps to distinguish the two candidates on the ballot. In Washington state, the Justice Department on Monday [USN:L6N46D0UP TEXT:"sent a letter"] asking officials not to count any ballots received from 400 voters it said may not be citizens. Washington's top elections official said the timing of the request indicated it was intended to cast unfounded suspicion on election results. California had 23 million registered voters as of December 2025, while Washington had 5 million registered voters as of 2024, state records show. Voting rights activists have expressed concern that the federal government's methods for scrutinizing state voter lists to identify noncitizen voters risk wrongly flagging naturalized citizens for removal from the rolls.

NEW YORK, Oct 27 : A US regulator is investigating whether prediction market operator Polymarket violated a 2022 enforcement deal in which it promised to ban US users from its main overseas platform, reviving an inquiry the agency shuttered last year without bringing charges, said two people familiar with the matter. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is probing whether Polymarket took sufficient steps to keep US users off the platform as part of a broader investigation it opened into the company earlier this year, the people said. One of the people said the scrutiny is focused on Polymarket's past controls and processes. The agency is examining Polymarket's controls for determining where customers are located, as well as its advertising activities in the United States, as part of that inquiry, the people said. Polymarket is based in New York and has an offshore entity registered in Panama.

The CFTC is also scrutinizing Polymarket's US platform, which the company began rolling out late last year, including its customer onboarding processes and customer protections, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential enforcement issues. Reuters is reporting these elements of the probe for the first time. The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg News and other media first reported in June that the CFTC was broadly probing Polymarket, but provided few details. Bloomberg added that the CFTC was looking into social media activity tied to the company. Spokespeople for the CFTC and Polymarket declined to comment. Probes are not necessarily an indication of wrongdoing and many do not result in enforcement action.  The new details, nevertheless, raise fresh questions over why the CFTC and Justice Department last year closed similar probes into whether Polymarket had violated the 2022 settlement, which resolved CFTC allegations at the time that Polymarket had been operating in the US unlawfully since its launch in 2020.  Neither agency has commented on the decision to close the probes and a Justice Department spokesperson declined to comment for this story. Prediction markets allow traders to bet on real-world events, including sports, government policy announcements and elections. Aided by supportive policies under President Donald Trump's second administration, the industry has surged over the past two years. Trump's son, Donald Trump Jr, is a Polymarket investor.  As the platforms have grown, they have drawn scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers and advocacy groups worried the platforms are creating new avenues for insider trading, while recent political upsets, including in Brazil this week, have raised questions about their accuracy. Polymarket has said it has revamped controls. The firm says it expressly prohibits the use of virtual private networks (VPNs) or similar tools to circumvent its geographic restrictions, and has extensive controls to monitor for misconduct and to prevent restricted users from accessing its offshore platform.  Speaking to Reuters in August, Shana Bautista, Polymarket's global head of investigations and intelligence, said US users circumventing its restrictions was not "a really prevalent issue."  BIDEN ADMINISTRATION AGENCIES OPENED PROBE IN 2024 Under the 2022 settlement negotiated by the CFTC's former Biden-era leadership, Polymarket agreed to stop offering its market to US users. But as 2024 US election bets on the platform grew, political pundits and social media users questioned whether Americans were circumventing Polymarket's restrictions.   Months before the election, the CFTC opened a probe into whether Polymarket was complying with the deal, Reuters and other media reported at the time. The Justice Department opened a related investigation, with the FBI searching Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan's New York home in November 2024. Two months later, the Trump administration took office and appointed new leaders to both agencies. On July 15, 2025, Coplan said in an X post that the CFTC and Justice Department had closed their probes and cleared the company of any wrongdoing. A week later, Polymarket said it had bought a CFTC-licensed derivatives exchange, which became the platform for its US operation. CFTC-registered platforms must comply with certain customer protection and market abuse prevention requirements. While CFTC data shows the agency's overall enforcement activity has slumped during Trump's second presidency, its enforcement director David Miller said during his first month on the job in March that he would aggressively police prediction markets.  In April, the agency and Justice Department charged a US soldier, alleging he made $400,000 from insider bets on Polymarket's offshore platform, sparking fresh questions about its controls.  According to the indictment, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who has pleaded not guilty, accessed the platform using a VPN and "exit mode," which geolocated to a foreign country. Polymarket said at the time that it had referred the matter to the authorities.

item.title: Trump promotes oil production in Texas, where Democrats dream of breakthrough
item.description: President Donald Trump campaigned in the traditionally solidly Republican state of Texas on Tuesday, seeking to boost US Senate candidate Ken Paxton and other party members and fend off what could be the first statewide Democratic victory in 32 years.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump campaigned in the traditionally solidly Republican state of Texas on Tuesday, seeking to boost US Senate candidate Ken Paxton and other party members and fend off what could be the first statewide Democratic victory in 32 years. With high fuel prices weighing heavily on the campaign for November 3 congressional elections, Trump scheduled a pair of stops at opposite ends of the oil-producing state. He appeared before a tanker containing Venezuelan crude in the Gulf of Mexico, and announced the easing of methane rules for oil and gas producers during a later stop in the West Texas city of Lubbock. "Tonight, I'm officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers $45 billion in costs, unlock vast quantities of Texas natural gas and produce 210 million barrels of oil," Trump said. Trump sought to show voters he was working to bring down gasoline prices a week before the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"], when the balance of power in Congress will be at stake. Polls show the Democrats may retake control of one or both houses from the president's Republicans. Trump has taken a number of steps to [USN:L1N4670FM TEXT:"address fuel prices"], which have become a political liability for Republicans amid the US war with Iran. The trip marks Trump's third visit to Texas this month to mobilize support for Paxton, who is locked in a close race with Democrat James Talarico. A loss in Texas next Tuesday would complicate the Republican Party's path to retaining its slim Senate majority. The rally took place within view of an oil tanker, moored near the Port of Corpus Christi, that Trump said was loaded with the first oil received from Venezuela under a deal that Washington made after deposing the country's former leader. "We're celebrating the greatest oil victory in history. To the victor belongs the spoils, right?" Trump said. Texas has long been one of the main refining centers for Venezuelan crude oil. [USN:FWN44P1ZC TEXT:"Trump announced in August an agreement"] that grants the US access to a fifth of Venezuela's crude reserves. The White House said in September that oil from the deal would probably hit US reserves in November. The oil is slated to head to refineries owned by ExxonMobil and Citgo, a White House official told Reuters. LATE PUSH FOR PAXTON Texas has consistently voted Republican for 30 years, but Democrats raised their hopes this year when Paxton won the Senate nomination with Trump's backing. Paxton was indicted on securities-fraud charges in 2015 and impeached by the Texas House in 2023. The criminal case was dismissed in 2024 after an agreement with prosecutors, and the Texas Senate acquitted him in the impeachment trial. Trump has publicly criticized his longtime ally Paxton, calling him "a pain in the ass sometimes." He also heavily criticized Talarico, whom he accused of opposing Texas values on issues such as oil production, immigration and transgender rights. Tech billionaire Elon Musk and other donors are [USN:L6N4660XW TEXT:"pouring hundreds of millions"] into a late effort to rescue Paxton's campaign. "Our policy has always been drill, baby, drill. And man, we are drilling now. But if Texas elects Communist James 'Talafreako,' that wealth will rapidly disappear," Trump said, applying his preferred nickname to the Democratic candidate. Talarico has used the nickname as a fundraising tool, selling 'I'm a Talafreako' T-shirts, while also responding, "We are a threat to their corrupt system." During a later stop in Lubbock, Trump announced an Environmental Protection Agency proposal to roll back Biden-era rules that required companies to fix leaky equipment and regularly check wells for escaping methane, a potent greenhouse gas, the White House official said. The administration is casting it as a way to produce more energy and lower costs. The plan would give relief to small, low-output wells and end a program that used outside groups to report large methane leaks, the official said. It would also ease rules aimed at phasing out the routine burning off of gas at oil wells. Trump's repeated trips to Texas are part of a broader push in Republican-leaning states, which were expected to be safely in hand but have instead become midterm battlegrounds. His October campaign blitz has also taken him to Oklahoma, Alabama, Nebraska, Iowa, Ohio, South Carolina and Mississippi.

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo will meet with survivors of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy during his Nov 6 to 17 three-country tour of South America , the Vatican said on Tuesday (Oct 27). The pontiff , who is recovering from lung cancer surgery , will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on one of the most intense foreign trips taken by a pope in decades, after being deemed fit for the journey by his doctor on Monday. "Several meet ings are planned with people who have been victims of abuse by members of the clergy and the Church," the Vatican said in its Tuesday statement. "These meet ings reflect the pope 's desire to express his closeness to those who have suffered, and who still suffer, because of this violence," it said. Pope Leo , 71, has held meet ings with survivors of abuse by clergy on several of his foreign visits, including in France last month. In that encounter, the pope met for two hours with seven French victims and reaffirmed his commitment to ending abuse of children by Catholic priests, the Vatican said afterwards. Pope Leo , originally from the US, served as a missionary and bishop in Peru for decades before becoming the head of the Catholic Church .

LONDON: GSK said on Tuesday (Oct 27) that it expects to almost double the number of cancer medicines it has in clinical trials next year , including those in early-stage studies, as it tries to rebuild its oncology business. The drugmaker's clinical -stage portfolio of about 15 assets would likely "come close to doubling" in 2027, Hesham Abdullah, who heads GSK 's oncology research and development, told the Wall Street Journal earlier on Tuesday. The British drugmaker has bet big on cancer drugs under CEO Luke Miels, including its US$10.6 billion takeover of US biotech Nuvalent earlier this year . One of the drugs acquired in the process received approval in July while a regulatory decision on another is expected by November. Miels faces the task of reassuring investors that the company can navigate looming patent cliffs for its blockbuster HIV drugs.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro and family to receive US visas after leaving Brazil, State Department says
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election, three sources said, with the US State Department due to grant him and his family entry visas.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Gram Slattery, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election, three sources said, with the US State Department due to grant him and his family entry visas. Bolsonaro, who has yet to concede to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, left Brazil after refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports. The ruling relates to a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing. The location of Flavio, his wife and two daughters was not immediately clear. One source close to the family said Flavio had landed in Florida, but declined to say where. "The State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States," a senior State Department official said. BRAZIL-US RIFT GROWS Bolsonaro's departure threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas. Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to put them back in power, and Reuters reported ahead of Sunday's election on [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"a US State Department"] campaign to restore them to office. US President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that he would approve of Flavio Bolsonaro coming to the United States. "Well, I would approve. I think they're fine people. The election was very strange, and I thought it was terrible. It's gotten bad reviews. You look at what happened to their market", Trump said. "I think it's so terrible to see it. I didn't take sides, you know. I know them both. I know Lula. I know Flavio a little bit. I know the father very well. The father was treated really badly. I thought, but I wasn't involved. That's Brazil. It's a different country", he said. Trump has previously alleged Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil. The elder Bolsonaro also went to the United States after refusing to concede to Lula in 2022, when former US President Joe Biden was in office. He eventually returned but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia. Lula, speaking in Brasilia, said he had just heard that Flavio had left the country, and called it shameful, saying he should have stayed in Brazil and proved his innocence. Bolsonaro had been favored to win Sunday's presidential election but ended up [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"losing"] in a shock result. ORDERED TO HAND OVER PASSPORTS On Monday, he was given 24 hours to surrender his passports, which were canceled after the deadline lapsed, two sources said. In a court ruling seen by Reuters, the Supreme Court cited the risk of Bolsonaro fleeing Brazil and his "significant financial resources" in ordering his passports seized. Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, had said on Monday he had no plans to flee. "I have never thought about leaving the country," he said. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me." His departure appeared to have caught his campaign manager off guard. "We are surprised by the news because, just yesterday, we discussed the need for Flavio — given the 60 million votes he received — to take on this role as leader of the opposition," Senator Rogerio Marinho told reporters. FOLLOWING FATHER'S PATH Although Bolsonaro has yet to officially concede defeat — saying on Sunday he would seek the annulment of the result over alleged voter irregularities — his Liberal Party said on Monday it acknowledged Lula's victory. It remains unclear how Bolsonaro was able to leave the country while he was facing a 24-hour deadline to hand over his passports. A senior Federal Police official said Bolsonaro had not exited the country via any regular migration point. Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro's younger brother who lives in the United States, said ahead of the vote that an election loss would require a move. "If my brother does not win, I'm in favor that he would leave the country," he told podcaster Steven Crowder this month.

item.title: Canada, UAE sign trade deal as Carney seeks new trading partners
item.description: Canada and the United Arab Emirates signed a comprehensive trade deal on Tuesday to lower barriers between the two economies and boost investment, the governments said, as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to expand trade and investment ties at a time of tension with the United States.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: (This Oct 27 story has been corrected to restore the deleted text '$50 billion in investment' in paragraph 10.) Canada and the United Arab Emirates signed a comprehensive trade deal on Tuesday to lower barriers between the two economies and boost investment, the governments said, as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to expand trade and investment ties at a time of tension with the United States. Carney and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan presided over the signing of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which aims to cut tariffs, reduce red tape and improve market access for businesses in both countries. Carney has vowed to double Canada's non-US trade over the next decade as President Donald Trump's tariffs have rippled through Canada's economy. Subsequent attempts for a deal with Washington have broken down, and that has pushed Carney to aggressively pursue trade pacts with countries from the Asia Pacific to Europe and Middle East. "Once fully implemented, the CEPA will reduce or eliminate tariffs on over 99% of current Canadian exports to the UAE. That means new markets for Canadian farmers growing pulses and canola, for manufacturers of industrial machinery and power generation equipment, for our world-class aerospace sector, and other Canadian innovators," The Prime Minister's Office said in a statement. "The agreement will also address non-tariff barriers, create a more predictable environment for trade and investment, and expand market access for Canadian goods and services, including in the industrial, agricultural, forest, fish and seafood, environmental, and engineering sectors," it said, adding CEPA is expected to enter into force in 2027. The two countries also signed preliminary agreements on energy, diplomatic and defence cooperation. "We see considerable potential for our private sector, whether through improved market access for our exporters or access to investment opportunities in high-growth sectors such as logistics, communications, advanced technology and manufacturing – all of which will support our pursuit of a resilient, diversified and globally connected economy,” UAE's Foreign Trade Minister Thani Al Zeyoudi said in a statement. He signed the CEPA deal with his Canadian counterpart Maninder Sidhu. UAE is the largest Middle Eastern market for Canadian exports and is a big buyer of Canadian motor vehicles and parts, and machinery. Two-way trade between the countries was worth C$3.5 billion ($2.48 billion) last year. It has been growing at 10% annually for the last few years, according to a government data. The UAE last year also committed up to $50 billion in investment in Canada. The signing is the last step before Canada’s Parliament can ratify the agreement, a Canadian government source said.

item.title: 米ＵＰＳ、7─9月期は利益が予想上回る 通期見通し上方修正
item.description:
Nandan Mandayam Lisa Baertlein
[２７日 ロイター] - 国際貨物輸送大手の米ユナイテッ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ＵＰＳ、7─9月期は利益が予想上回る　通期見通し上方修正 0:30 配信

米ＵＰＳの電気配送トラック。2023年9月、カリフォルニア州コンプトンで撮影。REUTERS/Lisa Baertlein（ロイター） Nandan Mandayam　Lisa Baertlein

[２７日 ロイター] - 国際貨物輸送大手の米ユナイテッド・パーセル・サービス（ＵＰＳ）が２７日発表した２０２６年７─９月期決算は、１株当たり調整後利益が１．６９ドルだった。前年同期の１．７４ドルを下回ったものの、ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想の１．６３ドルを上回った。コスト削減効果に加え、利益率の高い国際航空輸送が寄与した。同時に、２６年１２月期通期の売上高と利益の見通しを上方修正した。

２６年７─９月期は、売上高の約６割を占める米国内部門の調整後営業利益率が７．０％と、前年同期の６．４％から伸びた。国際部門は１４．９％と、前年同期の１４．８％からわずかに上昇した。

２６年通期のコスト削減目標３０億ドルの達成に向け順調に推移し、２６年９月までに１８億ドルを削減したと説明した。複数の施設を閉鎖したほか、人員削減を進めてきた。米アマゾン・ドット・コム向け戸口配送については、第２・四半期（４─６月）に縮小が完了した。

通期の１株当たり調整後利益見通しは約７．２８ドルと、７月時点の７．２２ドルから上方修正。市場予想は７．１９ドルだった。通期売上高見通しは９２６億ドルとし、従来予想の９１２億ドルから引き上げた。市場予想の９１７億３０００万ドルを上回る水準を予想した。

同業の米フェデックスは２８日に決算を発表する。

item.title: 米新築住宅販売、9月は0.6％減の67.6万戸 金利上昇で需要低迷
item.description: [ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - 米商務省が２７日発表した９月の新築一戸建て住宅販売戸数（季節調整済み）は年率換...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米新築住宅販売、9月は0.6％減の67.6万戸　金利上昇で需要低迷 0:19 配信

米カリフォルニア州カールスバッドにある住宅に掲げられた「売家」の看板。９月撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake（ロイター） [ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - 米商務省が２７日発表した９月の新築一戸建て住宅販売戸数（季節調整済み）は年率換算で前月比０．６％減の６７万６０００戸となった。中東紛争を背景とした住宅ローン金利の上昇が需要を押し下げた。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は６５万戸だった。前年同月比では５．３％減少した。

８月分は６８万戸と、当初発表の６８万４０００戸から下方改定された。

３０年固定住宅ローン平均金利は、米国とイスラエルが２月末にイランを攻撃して以降、１３０ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）超上昇している。 住宅金融機関フレディマックのデータによると、同平均金利は先週、７．３２％となった。

９月は地域別では中西部と南部で減少した一方、北東部と西部で急増した。

新築住宅価格の中央値は前年同月比３．９％下落の４０万０４００ドル。９月に販売された住宅の大半は４９万９９９９ドル以下の価格帯だった。

新築住宅在庫は４７万６０００戸と、８月の４８万１０００戸から減少した。

９月の販売ペースに基づく在庫の消化期間は８．４カ月。８月は８．５カ月だった。

item.title: 米住宅価格指数、8月は前月比0.3％上昇＝ＦＨＦＡ
item.description: [ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - 米連邦住宅金融庁（ＦＨＦＡ）が２７日発表した８月の米住宅価格指数（季節調整済み...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米住宅価格指数、8月は前月比0.3％上昇＝ＦＨＦＡ 0:00 配信

2026年9月16日、米カリフォルニア州で撮影。 REUTERS/Mike Blake/File Photo（ロイター） [ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - 米連邦住宅金融庁（ＦＨＦＡ）が２７日発表した８月の米住宅価格指数（季節調整済み）は前月比０．３％上昇した。住宅ローン金利の上昇が住宅需要を圧迫しているものの、価格は上昇を続けた。７月の前月比は当初の０．３％上昇から０．２％上昇に下方改定された。

前年同月比では２．４％上昇と、７月の２．５％から伸びが鈍化した。

地域別では、前月比で９地域のうち５地域が上昇。東南中部地域が２．１％上昇したほか、西北中部、西南中部、東北中部の各地域でも堅調に上昇した。一方、ニューイングランド地域は０．８％低下し、中部大西洋岸地域は横ばいだった。

前年同月比では全９地域が上昇。東北中部地域が４．４％上昇と急伸した。

住宅ローン金利と住宅価格の上昇は、１１月３日の中間選挙を前に選挙戦の中心的なテーマとなっている。

住宅金融機関フレディマックのデータによると、主力の３０年固定住宅ローン平均金利は先週７．３２％となった。小幅に低下したものの、２月末の米・イランの戦争開始以降、上昇幅は１４０ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）を超えている。

item.title: 米10月ＣＢ消費者信頼感、91.7に上昇 ガソリン安で改善
item.description: [ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - 米民間調査機関コンファレンス・ボード（ＣＢ）が２７日発表した１０月の消費者信頼感...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米10月ＣＢ消費者信頼感、91.7に上昇　ガソリン安で改善 10/27 23:50 配信

１０月２１日、米カリフォルニア州で撮影　REUTERS/Mike Blake（ロイター） [ワシントン　２７日　ロイター] - 米民間調査機関コンファレンス・ボード（ＣＢ）が２７日発表した１０月の消費者信頼感指数は９１．７と、９月の改定値８４．２から上昇した。ガソリン価格の低下を背景に消費者心理が改善した。ただ、生活費の上昇に対する不満が根強いことも分かった。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は８１．０だった。９月の指数は当初発表の８１．９から上方改定された。

職が「十分」と「就職困難」の回答から算出する労働市場格差は５．３％と、９月の２．９％から拡大した。

消費者は今後６カ月間、サービスや耐久財への支出を削減する予定だと回答。一方、住宅の購入を予定する消費者の割合は増えた。

ＣＢのグローバル指標担当シニアエコノミスト、ファーガス・マコーミック氏は「今回の回復は、９月から１０月にかけてみられたガソリン小売価格の低下と整合している」と指摘。ただ「１０月の自由記述回答では、物価上昇に対する不満が引き続き示された。価格上昇や食品・日用品価格の高さ、原油やディーゼル燃料価格に関する言及が増加している」と述べた。

ロイター 関連リンク 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：米長期金利5％接近で株式市場に警戒感、決算後はマクロ要因に注目 焦点：ベセント氏発言で強まる日銀9月利上げ観測、米国の影響力拡大に懸念も アングル：米国債「ツイスト・スティープ化」、ＦＲＢの信認巡る懸念反映か アングル：インフレで揺らぐ債券のヘッジ機能、米投資家は実物資産に移行 10/28(水) 3:38 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: Palestinians protest against military demolitions in West Bank as Israelis vote
item.description: Over 3,000 Palestinians had been forced from their homes by the Israeli military operation, which targeted neighborhoods near the checkpoint where Palestinian gunmen killed the two Israeli soldiers on Oct 23, the United Nations said.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Palestinians protest against military demolitions in West Bank as Israelis vote

Over 3,000 Palestinians had been forced from their homes by the Israeli military operation, which targeted neighborhoods near the checkpoint where Palestinian gunmen killed the two Israeli soldiers on Oct 23, the United Nations said.

Palestinians argue with Israeli army soldiers during a protest of Palestinian residents against their displacement from a neighbourhood, amid ongoing Israeli military operations, in Hebron in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct 27, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Mussa Qawasma)

HEBRON, West Bank: Israeli troops fired a stun grenade on Tuesday (Oct 27) to disperse Palestinians who gathered to protest against an Israeli military operation that has displaced thousands of residents from a neighbourhood in Hebron in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. The unrest, which follows the deaths of two Israeli soldiers shot by Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint last week, unfolded as Israelis were voting in an election in which the country's posture in the West Bank has been a major political issue. Some Palestinian officials have accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of launching a crackdown in the West Bank to coincide with the vote, as a way to energise his right-wing supporters. The government says its operation is a response to the attack on its soldiers. A group of Palestinian men, women and children gathered at Tuesday's protest. One elderly man held a placard that said: "No to collective punishment, no to closures, and no to displacement."

The military said it had fired a stun grenade to disperse them so that its operation could continue.

A Palestinian man holds a placard which reads: "No to collective punishment / No to closure and no to displacement" during a protest in Hebron in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct 27, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Mussa Qawasma)

On Monday, the United Nations said that over 3,000 Palestinians had been forced from their homes by the Israeli military operation, which targeted neighborhoods near the checkpoint where Palestinian gunmen killed the two Israeli soldiers on Friday. "Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law," said UN human rights chief Volker Türk in a statement. "Threats to empty and erase entire neighbourhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing." The Israeli military said in a statement on Sunday that troops would carry out demolitions in the area. It said soldiers had not located any weapons in searches of the houses. Since Friday's attack on the checkpoint, Israel has blocked the entrances to most Palestinian cities and towns across the West Bank, severely curtailing Palestinians' freedom of movement. Noura Nassar, a displaced resident who attended the protests, said she had struggled to get medical treatment because of the blockages. "Where is the democracy in all of this? Their elections are today, sure, but what about us? Aren't we human beings? We want to go out, we want to visit the doctor," said Nassar.

A child looks at a banner depicting Israeli Prime Minister and Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu, during the country's national elections in Jerusalem, Oct 27, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Ronen Zvulun)

Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot both oppose the creation of an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. Residents expelled from the Hebron neighbourhood said Tuesday's election in Israel would do little to change the reality on the ground in territories Israel has occupied since 1967. "Among themselves they will elect who is the oppressor and who will destroy the Palestinian people. That is their election," said Sana' Salman Abu Sneineh, another expelled resident. Netanyahu's government has presided over a rapid expansion of Israeli settlements, which are deemed illegal by UN bodies and most countries, though Israel disputes this. Under Netanyahu's right-wing coalition there has also been a surge of militant settler violence against Palestinians.

Related:

Israel election: Voting underway in first poll since 7 Oct 2023 Hamas attack

Fastest turnout in 45 years as Israelis pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu

Source: Reuters/cc

item.title: Syngenta targets valuation of at least $66 billion in Hong Kong IPO, people say
item.description: Syngenta's advisers are targeting a valuation of at least $66 billion in the Swiss-Chinese agrochemicals group's planned Hong Kong listing, which is likely to take place early next year, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: John Revill, Oliver Hirt
item.content:encoded: Syngenta's advisers are targeting a valuation of at least $66 billion in the Swiss-Chinese agrochemicals group's planned Hong Kong listing, which is likely to take place early next year, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters. UBS (UBSG.S) and China International Capital Corp (CICC), two of Syngenta's IPO sponsor banks, are marketing the Basel-based maker of seeds and crop-protection products at 15 to 20 times expected 2026 core earnings (EBITDA), the people said. That would value Syngenta, which is controlled by Chinese state-owned firm Sinochem (600500.SS) , at $66 billion to $88 billion, based on its 2025 EBITDA of $4.4 billion, placing the offering among the largest global IPOs expected next year. The valuation reflects Syngenta's efforts to position itself more as a biotechnology company than as a chemicals producer, the people said. One of them added that a strong product lineup in crop protection and a development pipeline for new seed varieties resistant to disease and pests supported a high valuation. China CITIC Bank and Bank of America are also sponsors of the IPO, said a separate source with knowledge of the offering. Syngenta and UBS declined to comment. CICC, China CITIC Bank and Bank of America did not respond to requests for comment. JANUARY WINDOW Three people said the IPO could still take place before the end of 2026, but an early-2027 debut was considered more likely. "There's confidence a January window is feasible," said one. The bankers are meeting investors in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Beijing ahead of planned marketing in Frankfurt and London. Some Asian investors are also showing renewed interest in more traditional industrial companies as enthusiasm for AI-related stocks cools, the people added. Syngenta plans to sell a stake of 10% to 20% and use the [USN:L1N3Z10GT TEXT:"proceeds"] to reduce debt and invest in crop-protection products and seeds. The company has already [USN:L4N4570NW TEXT:"filed"] for the flotation, which could raise $5 billion to $10 billion. Hong Kong's IPO market is booming, with 118 newly listed companies raising HK$388.0 billion ($49.5 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, up 106% from a year earlier, according to HKEX data. Sentiment weakened this month, however, after a selloff in [USN:L6N46C0R0 TEXT:"AI-related stocks"] raised concerns over valuations and returns on AI spending. Changzhou Microintelligence and Jiangsu Slender West Lake Culture and Tourism [USN:L3N46C0CM TEXT:"postponed"] their offerings, citing [USN:FWN4660V7 TEXT:"market conditions"]. ChemChina Group [USN:KBN1810CM TEXT:"acquired Syngenta for $43 billion"] in 2017 in what is China's largest foreign takeover to date, before the group itself was [USN:L1N2LT16F TEXT:"merged into Sinochem"] in 2021 to create the world's biggest industrial chemicals company. Syngenta's IPO would revive Sinochem's efforts to take the company public after it withdrew a proposed Shanghai listing in 2024. Syngenta competes with BASF (BASFn.DE) , Bayer (BAYGn.DE) and Corteva (CTVA.N) , and recently appointed as CEO Hengde Qin, a Chinese national seen as someone who can navigate the various approval processes. The company sells seeds, herbicides, insecticides and fungicides, alongside biological and digital farming products. It has more than 50,000 employees in over 90 countries, according to its website.

item.title: Lula's win in Brazil deals harsh blow to Trump’s ‘Donroe Doctrine’
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise reelection victory on Sunday dealt a harsh blow to US President Donald Trump’s Donroe Doctrine, a plan to secure a US "sphere of influence" in the Americas against growing Chinese influence. The question now is just how much Brazil will tilt toward Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's [USN:L6N4681ER TEXT:"surprise reelection victory"] on Sunday dealt a harsh blow to US President Donald Trump’s [USN:L1N43A0RG TEXT:""Donroe Doctrine,""] a plan to secure a US "sphere of influence" in the Americas against growing Chinese influence. The question now is just how much Brazil will tilt toward Beijing. Trump's grand plans at the start of the year to solidify Washington's influence over Latin America were epitomized by US forces' extraordinary [USN:L6N3Y407K TEXT:"capture and extradition"] of Venezuela's leftist President Nicolas Maduro on January 3. Lula's victory has thrown a spanner in the works. South America's most populous nation will be led for another four years by the [USN:L6N46B06R TEXT:"veteran leftist"] and long-standing critic of US influence. Trump [USN:L6N46C02Y TEXT:"said on Monday"] that he likes Lula and gets along well with him, but it's safe to say he would have had a more cordial relationship with Lula’s right-wing opponent, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. What makes Lula's win even more vexing for Washington is that it is likely to strengthen Brazil's ties with China, a process that Lula has long championed. China overtook the US as Brazil's largest trading partner in 2009. Officially, Lula will avoid aligning himself too closely with either superpower. "We are no one's backyard!" Lula told thousands of supporters at his victory rally in Sao Paulo on Sunday. That could be interpreted as a warning to the US and China that Brazil will not be bullied into relinquishing control of its vast resources, from energy and minerals to the Amazon rainforest. But "backyard" clearly sounds like a nod to the US. Trump's "Donroe Doctrine," a revival of the 200-year-old "Monroe Doctrine" that claimed the US should have a "zone of influence" in the Americas, has not been particularly well received in Latin America. A victory for Trump's political ally Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday would likely have strengthened Washington's plans in the region, which may have pushed other countries to trim ties with Beijing. But with Lula's continued tenure, the White House may need to focus more on damage control. "Lula’s victory certainly reinforces Brazil’s economic relationship with China," says Emanuel Ornelas, a professor at the Sao Paulo School of Economics-FGV. For a White House intent on expanding US influence at China’s expense, that is worrisome. CHINA’S GROWING FOOTPRINT As the battle between the US and China for global economic supremacy ratchets up amid an escalating AI arms race, securing a reliable supply of energy, resources and materials has become more important than ever. Brazil sits across all of those areas. Brazil holds around 20% of global rare earth reserves and is a major producer of a range of minerals critical to technologies like semiconductors, renewable energy, robotics and defense applications. Its resources are a key part of global supply chains, and the country is also an agricultural powerhouse, supplying the world with around 27% of its sugarcane, 25% of its soybeans, 9% of its cotton, and 6% of its beef and corn. China already has a distinct advantage. Brazil currently exports around three times as much to China as it does to the US, in dollar terms, and imports around twice as much from the Asian superpower as it does from America. This gap is widening. Trump's tariffs pushed China to increasingly replace US agricultural goods with Brazilian alternatives. The war in the Middle East has also tightened trade ties between Brasilia and Beijing by disrupting normal energy trade patterns. Crude oil now rivals soybeans as Brazil’s largest export and has helped fill the gap created by shuttered Middle East production. China is the largest buyer of both. While Brazil plays a multifaceted role in US plans to remain the world’s main superpower, China's view of Brazil appears more straightforward. It wants access to the commodities, energy and minerals needed to sustain its industrial base, which increasingly includes high-value manufacturing. Will Lula have a strong enough hand to secure advantageous terms with the US and China as they seek access to Brazil's resources? This could prove challenging. He faces many hurdles at home, including a high likelihood of legislative gridlock in Brasilia. Markets don't seem enthused either. While the [USN:L6N46C031 TEXT:"historic plunge"] in Brazilian markets (.BVSP) , on Monday following Lula's win was exaggerated, it was telling nonetheless: investors appear very skeptical about the country's fiscal outlook and economic growth prospects. What happens matters beyond the country’s borders. Brazil, in UniCredit’s words, is both a "strategic resource power" and a "geopolitical swing state" in the US-China rivalry. Which side will prevail? That remains a toss-up. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? item.title: Iran says Sinokor vessels face legal action; South Korean shipowners deny link
item.description: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a body set up by Tehran to manage passage requests in the Strait of Hormuz, said on Tuesday all vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor [RIC:RIC:SINKM.UL] would face "legal action" starting on November 1.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a body set up by Tehran to manage passage requests in the Strait of Hormuz, said on Tuesday all vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor [RIC:RIC:SINKM.UL] would face "legal action" starting on November 1. Tehran has sought to tighten its grip on the strategic waterway by attacking shipping there since US and Israeli airstrikes on Iran on February 28. It has restricted transit to try to gain leverage over Washington, while disrupting oil flows from Arab Gulf oil producers, especially to their customers in Asia. The authority said on X that Sinokor vessels had committed the highest number of crossing violations in the strait over the past three months, and "appropriate actions" had been taken against at least seven of them. The Korea Shipowners' Association said on Wednesday the vessels in question were not owned by Sinokor but had been sub-chartered to an overseas oil company, and had no South Korean crew, with only foreign seafarers on board. The association said it had confirmed this through a Sinokor official. Sinokor was unaware of the authority's separate warning of legal action and was checking the details, the association said. Ships owned by Sinokor were previously included on a [USN:L1N44L07X TEXT:"list issued by Iran"] in August of 45 tankers that it said had broken its rules for crossing the Strait of Hormuz. In response to Iranian attacks, the United States also imposed a naval blockade against ships linked to the Islamic Republic in the strait. While the blockade has all but choked off Iranian exports, Gulf producers have adapted to attacks on shipping by relying on so-called dark transits — switching off tankers' tracking systems to evade detection — to protect the oil flows that underpin their economies.

item.title: India economic growth seen losing momentum after strong start to fiscal year: Reuters poll
item.description: Economic growth in India is forecast to have slowed this fiscal year from a surprisingly strong pace and hover around 7% over the forecast horizon as higher energy costs add to near-term inflation risks, a Reuters poll of economists found.
item.dc:creator: Pranoy Krishna
item.content:encoded: Economic growth in India is forecast to have slowed this fiscal year from a surprisingly strong pace and hover around 7% over the forecast horizon as higher energy costs add to near-term inflation risks, a Reuters poll of economists found. The US-Israeli-led war with Iran has so far had limited impact on economic growth, but it has pushed up inflation mainly through higher energy costs. The Reserve Bank of India has [USN:L1N4670J9 TEXT:"raised rates"] once and is expected to do so twice more, to 6.0%, by end-March. But with no planned major policy changes, Asia's third-largest economy is forecast to carry on growing steadily at a rate most forecasters agree will not bring about any significant improvements in job prospects, particularly for young people. "7% growth is quite healthy, especially in this climate. But is that healthy for India? I would say it's probably just average," said Miguel Chanco, chief emerging Asia economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics. Gross domestic product was forecast to grow 7.1% in the fiscal year ending March 2027, according to the median estimate in an October 19-26 Reuters poll, down from 7.7% in FY 2025-26. Growth was then expected to ease to 7.0% in FY 2027-28. The forecast for this fiscal year was [USN:L1N45T036 TEXT:"in line"] with RBI expectations as well as an earlier Reuters survey and broadly matched that of the International Monetary Fund. Economists have underestimated India's growth in 10 of the past 12 quarters despite forecasts generally clustering within a narrow range close to 7%. JOBS OUTLOOK DIMS AS OIL, AI WEIGH Private investment, a key driver of job creation, [USN:L4N44S0T4 TEXT:"expanded"] by nearly 12% in the June quarter. Forecasters say sustaining such growth will become increasingly difficult if oil prices remain elevated. Crude oil futures are trading around $116 a barrel, about 60% above pre-war levels. India has also missed out on the surge in AI investment that has lifted growth in other Asian economies like South Korea. "India's caught between its own ... domestic issues of low, insufficient private investment growth, but also there's this global backdrop of AI making it unnecessary to hire as many entry-level positions," said Chanco. "It's causing a lot of dissatisfaction among the youth in India, and rightly so." A [USN:L1N45O03D TEXT:"student-led movement"] that began as online satire has spilled onto India's streets in recent months, reflecting growing concerns over education and jobs despite the country's rapid economic growth. Inflation is squeezing household budgets as savings dwindle. Price growth was forecast to average 6.1% this quarter and remain above the RBI's 4% medium-term target at least until end-2027. That outlook is slightly higher than the forecast in last month’s survey. "Stronger cost pass-through (from higher energy prices) and gradually rising services inflation increase the risk that elevated price pressures become embedded," wrote Kunal Kundu, India economist at Societe Generale. Households are at risk from future cuts to welfare spending, which has long helped support demand and protect millions from poverty, economists say. The 2026-27 budget projected a 4.5% cut in food, fertiliser and petroleum subsidies. "The fact not only the central government but state governments are also actually providing significant amounts of cash to protect consumption, which is basically all the schemes they are running, immediately tells me all is not well," said Indranil Pan, chief economist at Yes Bank. ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the October Reuters global economic poll)

item.title: Alleged Israeli spy company heavily targeted Starlink users, sources say
item.description: Experts at a digital defense firm recently found that an Israeli ad tech company was heavily targeting users of Starlink's satellite internet service in a likely effort to spy on them, according to six people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: Experts at a digital defense firm recently found that an Israeli ad tech company was heavily targeting users of Starlink's satellite internet service in a likely effort to spy on them, according to six people familiar with the matter. Researchers at TrendAI, a unit of Tokyo-based cybersecurity company Trend Micro (4704.T) , concluded the Israeli company Discover-Tech was one of the biggest sources of digital ads shown to users of SpaceX's Starlink service and that the ads were likely being used to geolocate or otherwise surveil them, according to the six people. The researchers, who drew on digital advertising data in TrendAI's telemetry for their conclusions, found that Discover-Tech had become one of the world’s leading bidders for ads aimed at Starlink users and that it was the No. 1 bidder on Starlink traffic in more than 100 countries, including several where Starlink itself was banned or restricted. Bidding refers to the complex auction system by which advertisers secure space inside people's browsers and apps. SpaceX (SPCX.O) did not respond to requests for comment. Discover-Tech and its chief executive did not respond to requests for comment over the past two weeks. TrendAI released a report on October 15 about the targeting of Starlink users but did not name Discover-Tech, instead saying the party responsible was “an ad tech entity” which it called “Shadow-Earth-79.” The six sources said Shadow-Earth-79 is TrendAI’s codename for Discover-Tech. TrendAI did not directly address questions about why its report did not identify Shadow-Earth-79 by name, saying in a statement that its approach to attribution was aimed at reducing the risk of mistakes and avoiding "hype-driven labels" or "unstable actor names that can mislead defenders, distort risk prioritization, and trigger inappropriate response actions." Finding ways to track Starlink users has become a cottage industry as governments around the world try to get a grip on the spread of satellite internet terminals. Because they route data through SpaceX-operated satellites rather than nationally regulated telecommunications firms, the terminals can sidestep local internet restrictions, communicate in hostile areas or coordinate action across battlefields. Starlink has become [USN:L5N46A00R TEXT:"a particularly important resource"] in Ukraine, whose military relies on the service [USN:L8N46213X TEXT:"for frontline communications"] and [USN:L8N4350JH TEXT:"directing drone strikes"]. In May, Israeli newspaper Haaretz and the website Intelligence Online separately reported that Israeli-owned businesses were pitching clients on ways to identify and track Starlink users. Haaretz said exploiting ad data appeared to play a key role in the process. DISCOVER-TECH ACCUSED OF WIDER SPY EFFORT The same day that TrendAI published its report on Shadow-Earth-79, Canadian cyber watchdog Citizen Lab and New York advertising technology firm Confiant [USN:L6N45Z04V TEXT:"outed Discover-Tech by name"]. Both groups said the Israeli company abused the ad bidding process, which can leak data about internet users back to the bidder. Over time, bidders can collect that leaked data, collate it and merge it with other information to de-anonymize users, follow them around the web and, in some cases, set them up for targeting with surveillance software. Citizen Lab and Confiant said the ads had been shown inside dozens of sensitive networks belonging to media organizations, governments and tech firms . In response to the investigations, Google, Comcast and other companies said they had removed Discover-Tech from their ad platforms. At least one big US tech company and one international organization recently launched internal inquiries into whether Discover-Tech's ads targeted their employees, according to one of the people and a seventh person familiar with the matter. TOP ADVERTISER IN YEMEN, SOUTH SUDAN TrendAI's report cited suspicious bidding patterns that suggested Shadow-Earth-79 was running "targeting and tracking infrastructure rather than a commercial advertising operation." In addition to noting the "obvious skew" towards buying ads aimed at Starlink users, the report said that Shadow-Earth-79 was the top buyer of ads in Syria, Libya, Yemen and South Sudan and was the No. 2 ad buyer in Afghanistan even though "the demand for legitimate Western advertising in sanctioned or active-conflict states is effectively zero." It said the entity won "an implausibly dominant share" of bids in several countries including Hungary, Israel, Egypt, Azerbaijan and Venezuela. TrendAI researchers were convinced Discover-Tech was behind the suspicious bidding activity and discussed naming the company in TrendAI's report, according to the six people familiar with the matter. But they eventually dropped the idea of publicly attributing the activity to a named company after TrendAI executives raised legal concerns, five of the sources said. Self-censorship is common in the cybersecurity industry, especially when executives fear that exposing surveillance operations could draw retribution, industry experts say. Earlier this year, US cybersecurity company Palo Alto stripped explicit references to China from a report on a global cyberespionage campaign even though its researchers were confident the hacking could be pinned on Beijing, [USN:L6N3Z714C TEXT:"Reuters reported at the time"]. Reuters said the report was watered down over fears that calling out China would cause problems for Palo Alto's operations there, which were already under scrutiny following a Beijing directive ordering domestic companies [USN:L1N3YF0B5 TEXT:"not to use its products"]. Palo Alto said the lack of attribution in its report was not correlated with "procurement regulations in China" and that any suggestion otherwise was "speculative and false."
